name: Boss BF-2 Flanger
description: This BOSS Flanger includes all the controls and flexibility of a pedal flanger and combines these characteristics with the technical perfection that distinguishes all BOSS effects. The BF-2 produces true flanging, pitch modulation, and vibrato effects with a wide range of control options, highest sound purity, and yet simple operation. One of its outstanding features is the high signal-to-noise ratio of more than -95dBm (IHF-A). The BOSS BF-2 Flanger offers quiet, clean operation and full functional flexibility, and has all the advantages of the BOSS compact format. The BF-2 contains a special BBD (Bucket Brigade Device) circuit that greatly reduces the noise associated with most electronic flangers. The BF-2's controls are Manual, Depth, Rate, and Resonance. The Manual control determines the delay time of the sound, with a range of 1 to 13 ms. By turning the Manual control fully to the left, the BF-2 acts as a non-sweep filter with adjustable equalization and ambient tonality. The Depth control sets the sweep range when the Manual control is in the 'min' position. The sweep speed can be adjusted with the Rate control from 100 ms to 16 s. The Flange effect can be intensified with the Resonance control by regenerating the signal. The BF-2's input impedance of 470 kOhm makes it ideally suited for guitar, bass, keyboards, as well as stage and studio mixing. In combination with its unmatched quality and flexibility, the BF-2 is one of the most universally applicable effect devices on the market.

name: Boss CE-1 Chorus Ensemble
description: The BOSS Chorus Ensemble is the originator of the chorus effect and, in its short lifespan, has already become "the" celebrity among effect pedals. For this reason, this effect is also copied by many other manufacturers. The CE-1 produces a lush and intense sonic texture that gives solo instruments a thick, deep sound, comparable to voice doubling - a "chorus" of voices. Furthermore, the CE-1 generates a vibrato effect. These effects are activated by two footswitches. One switches between normal and effect, the other footswitch switches between the Chorus and Vibrato effects. All functions are indicated by LEDs. The chorus effect's intensity is adjustable. Independently, there are two controls for vibrato: speed and vibrato depth. The CE-1 features stereo outputs, which, when connected to two amplifiers, create a large and wide chorus effect.

name: Boss CE-3 Chorus
description: The combination of the chorus effect, compactness, improved noise floor, dual power supply and FET switching of the popular CE-2 with stereo splitting and other remarkable features makes the CE-3 truly special. The CE-3 can produce a stereo effect from a mono signal via the two outputs A and B. The controls of the CE-3 are Delay, Rate and Depth, and there is also a switch for stereo mode. In Mode 1, both output jacks A and B output an effect plus a direct signal, but with a difference. In this mode, output A consists of the direct and effect signal of positive phase (direct signal + effect signal), while output B has the effect signal with negative phase (direct signal-effect signal). The two output jacks allow either the output of the entire effect to one amplifier or, when using two amplifiers, a true stereo chorus with a swirling, deep effect. In Mode II, the effect signal is only assigned to output A, while B outputs the unchanged signal. This Mode II configuration is also found in the well-known Roland Jazz Chorus amplifiers.

name: Boss CS-1 Compression Sustainer
description: The CS-1 Compression Sustainer is a compressor unit that produces clear and undistorted sound extensions. The wide compression range and high input level allow it to be used with any instrument. The controls on the CS-1 include volume level, sustain time, and a Normal/Treble boost switch. The volume control adjusts the output volume of the effect/normal, so that switching between normal and effect can be done without volume differences. The sustain control determines the degree of compression. When this control is turned clockwise to the stop, it means the longest sustain value. When moved in the opposite direction, the output level is limited. This is extremely useful for giving guitar or bass that final bite. An interesting feature of the CS-1 is the selector switch, which decides between normal and treble boost, for example to emphasize the higher frequency components in the sustain.

name: Boss NF-1 Noise Gate
description: The Noise Gate is an electronic device that suppresses unwanted background noise by muting the signal. Compared to other noise gates, the BOSS NF-1 stands out due to its high efficiency, without altering or coloring the sound of the connected instrument. The controls on the NF-1 Noise Gate are: Sensitivity and Decay (response time, muting after the last tone signal). The sensitivity setting determines the activation threshold. The second control is the time setting that should elapse after the last note until muting – the Decay Time. This makes it possible to accommodate any conceivable volume envelope of an instrument and allow it to fully express itself, without being limited by the noise gate. We don't notice it – but when we're not playing, there's no noise.

description: The NS-2 Noise Suppressor eliminates unwanted noise, especially that which builds up when using multiple effects units, without affecting the original sound characteristics or subtle nuances. name: Boss NS-2 Dynamic Filter Noise Suppressor
description: The NS-2 Noise Suppressor is a new noise reduction device that completely suppresses annoying noise, especially that which builds up when using multiple effects pedals. The NS-2 allows all sound characteristics of the original tone to pass through unaffected, preserving even the finest nuances. The sound remains pure and clear, allowing you to express your creativity 'undisturbed' by using all your effects pedals without interference, even for the most subtle sound nuances. For today's musician, for whom the use of various effects pedals has long become a necessity, the NS-2 will prove equally indispensable. Unlike conventional noise reduction devices, the NS-2 allows the tone decay to be adjusted to the signal level of the input signal. The result is effective noise suppression with a smooth fade-out that sounds as natural as if no noise reduction device were being used at all. A SEND and RETURN loop is built into the NS-2, preventing the level change problems that often occur when a conventional noise reduction device is connected at the end of an effects chain. Thanks to the SEND and RETURN loop, high stability is guaranteed under all operating conditions and at any point within the effects chain. The NS-2 features a separate DC OUT, which can power other effects pedals. Practical silent 'on-stage tuning' is also possible, as the NS-2's MUTE switch can be used as a tone kill switch.

The second important innovation of the OC-2 is the sound quality of the generated tone. The Octave produces two tones, one an octave lower and the second two octaves lower than the played note. name: Boss PSM-5 Power Supply & Master Switch
description: The PSM-5 is a stabilized power supply that can power up to five BOSS 9V effect pedals (or other compatible effect pedals). It operates on AC power. A PSA-series AC adapter is included for connection to a power outlet, ensuring trouble-free operation without the risk of depleted batteries. A parallel DC cable with five outputs is included, connecting to the rear of the PSM-5 and the power adapter jacks of the individual BOSS effect pedals. But the PSM-5 is much more than a common power supply; it can also be used simultaneously as a master switch. The Send jack on the left side of the PSM-5 connects to the first effect pedal in the chain. The output of the first effect pedal then connects to the input of the second, and so on. Finally, the last effect pedal in the chain connects to the Return jack on the right side of the PSM-5. The guitar (or other instrument) connects to the Guitar jack and the amplifier to the Amp jack of the PSM-5. These connections create two separate loops – one through the effect pedals, the other directly from the guitar to the amplifier, bypassing the effects. The loops can be easily selected by pressing the footswitch. An LED indicator illuminates when the effect loop is active. The remarkable PSM-5 enhances the performance of your effect pedals and controls them simultaneously – all in one enclosure.
keywords: Boss PSM-5 Power Supply & Master Switch

name: CE-2 Chorus
description: The CE-2 is the compact version of the famous CE-1 Chorus Ensemble pedal. Like the CE-1, the CE-2 offers the incomparable BOSS Chorus sound. One of the main reasons for the exceptional success of the chorus effect is its wide range of applications, from amplifying guitars, keyboards, and wind instruments to large vocal PAs. The controls on the CE-2 are 'Rate' (speed) and 'Depth' (effect depth). The CE-2 Chorus offers the well-known BOSS chorus effect, which provides a doubling or thickening effect, enriching the sound of guitars, keyboards, woodwind and brass instruments, and even vocals, without being obtrusive or distracting from the instrument's original tone. The CE-2 features controls for the depth of the chorus effect and the rate of its sweep for precise and creative control. The CE-2 Chorus also boasts one of the best signal-to-noise ratios among all compact effects units, over 90 dB, making it ideal for recording. Like other BOSS compact effects units, the CE-2 is equipped with quiet FET switching, LED on/off and battery indicator, a robust and reliable housing, and an AC adapter jack.

name: CH-1 SUPER Chorus
description: The CH-1 Super Chorus boasts all the advantages of BOSS's proven compact format. Unlike conventional chorus devices, however, this effect pedal allows for the creation of a wide variety of chorus effects. Punchy sounds with lots of presence are possible with the CH-1, as are the warm, sustained chorus effects found in so many popular songs. Characteristic of the CH-1 are its wide frequency response and high signal-to-noise ratio of 96 dB. The result of this sophisticated effect circuit is an exceptionally pure sound, comparable to the professional quality of much more expensive rack effects. Controls for effect level, EQ, modulation rate, and depth are used to create all desired chorus effects. Further features of the CH-1 include a separate stereo output. The effect pedal can be powered either by batteries or by an optionally available AC adapter (PSA series). Its versatility makes the CH-1 the ideal chorus pedal for any purpose and any musical style.
keywords: 9V battery or PSA-series AC adapter power supply

name: CS-1 Compression Sustainer
description: The CS-1 Compression Sustainer is a compressor unit that achieves clear and undistorted tone extensions. Its wide compression range and high input level allow it to be used with any instrument. Controls on the CS-1 include volume level, sustain time, and a selector switch for Normal/Treble boost. The volume level control balances the effect/normal output volume so that there are no volume differences when switching between normal and effect. The sustain control determines the compression level. Turning this knob clockwise to the stop provides the longest sustain value. Moving it in the opposite direction limits the output level. This is extremely useful for giving guitar or bass that extra bite. An interesting feature of the CS-1 is the selector switch, which chooses between normal and treble boost to, for example, emphasize higher frequency components in the sustain.

name: DC-3 Digital Dimension
description: From a 1986 Boss catalog: The DC-3 is a new Dimension pedal that operates entirely digitally, producing studio-quality chorus effects that far surpass those of conventional chorus units. The extraordinary effect capabilities of the DC-3 even extend beyond those of the popular DC-2 Dimension device. The chorus effect of the DC-3 sounds completely natural and is characterized by exceptionally high quality. Sounds processed by this Dimension device retain their entire character, including the finest nuances. Furthermore, the chorus effects of the DC-3 are absolutely free from the blurring that is unavoidable with conventional devices. The DC-3 is therefore the ideal effects unit for keyboards and guitars. The digital circuit of the DC-3 combines high-quality digital delay with digital modulation. This creates sound modulation with ideal two-phase synchronization, resulting in a natural-sounding dimension effect without fluctuations or blurring of the original sound. The surprisingly many effects can be easily adjusted with four controls: Effect Level, Equalizer, Rate, and Depth. Exceptional sound quality is guaranteed by the BOSS-developed LSI chip. This large-scale integrated circuit ensures crystal-clear sound without the slightest signal degradation. Since the signal is first routed through the equalizer and then through the chorus section, the sound can be considerably modified to produce soft to penetrating effects. As the DC-3 is equipped with two output jacks, a remarkably spacious and rich-sounding sound can be achieved. These output jacks also allow for the production of an impressive, dynamic stereo effect by connecting each output to a separate amplifier.
keywords: 9V battery or PSA-series AC adapter power supply

name: DM-1 Delay Machine
description: The DM-1, a compact echo device for foot operation, offers stepless delay time from 25 to 500 ms. The Intensity knob allows variation from simple echoes to multiple echoes. The Balance knob enables stepless mixing of direct and delayed signals. With separate outputs, a stereo effect can be produced when used with two amplifiers. The input sensitivity for microphone, guitar, keyboard, or mixer is adjusted by the Input Level switch. An LED indicates overload.
keywords: Intensity control for simple to multiple echoes
Balance control for stepless mix of direct and delayed signals
Separate outputs for stereo effect with two amplifiers
Input level switch for microphone, guitar, keyboard, or mixer

name: DS-2 TURBO Distortion
description: The DS-2 is a new distortion pedal featuring a Turbo circuit, enabling a wide range of distortion effects for various music styles. The DS-2's advanced technology ensures excellent sound quality at all settings. It produces sounds from soft saturation to hard distortion reminiscent of overdriven amplifier stacks. Turbo I mode creates a soft distortion effect with a linear frequency response, allowing for a clear, natural sound even at maximum instrument volume. Even with extreme settings, the sound remains musical and free of unpleasant harsh highs. In Turbo II mode, the DS-2 simulates the sound of an overdriven tube amplifier, emphasizing the mid-range of the sound spectrum to produce the powerful distortion sound indispensable in today's music scene. The DS-2 is the first BOSS compact effects unit with a remote jack. By connecting an external footswitch, such as the FS-5L, musicians can toggle between Turbo I and Turbo II modes, offering greater flexibility even in the middle of a song.
keywords: Turbo I mode (soft distortion, linear frequency response, clear sound)
Turbo II mode (simulates overdriven tube amp, mid-range emphasis, powerful distortion)
Remote jack for external footswitch (e.g., FS-5L) to switch between Turbo I/II
9V battery or AC adapter (PSA series) power
Equivalent input noise -120 dBm or less (IHF-A)

name: DS-330 GM Sound Module in Console Enclosure
description: The Boss DS-330 is a 28-voice GM digital synthesizer housed in a drum computer style enclosure. The sound generation is 16-part multitimbral, and the sounds are only very limitedly modifiable, as the DS-330 is based on Roland's SC-55 II sound module.
keywords: DS-330 GM Sound Module in Console Enclosure
Housed in a drum computer style enclosure
Sounds are only very limitedly modifiable
Based on Roland SC-55 II sound module

name: DSD-3 Digital Sampler/Delay
description: The DSD-3, with an extremely favorable price-performance ratio, can be used either as a digital sampling device or as a digital delay device. It contains a 12-bit A/D/A converter, achieving a frequency response of 40 Hz to 7 kHz. The DSD-3 enhances your creative possibilities for both recording and live performance. The sampling time can be set between 200 and 800 ms. There are two operating modes: Rec/Play and Play Only. In Rec/Play mode, recording and replay occur simultaneously. When the feedback control is set to maximum, it's possible to overdub another sample sound onto a previously recorded sound. In Play Only mode, the DSD-3 plays back the stored sample sound that was recorded in Rec/Play mode. Playback of the recorded sample sound is possible by pressing the pedal or by feeding an external trigger signal into the DSD-3. With the Time knob, the pitch of the recorded sample sound can be changed during playback. Additionally, the DSD-3 can be used as a digital delay device with a delay time of 50 to 800 ms. The delay time is determined by selecting S-mode (50 to 200 ms) or L-mode (200 to 800 ms) and turning the Time knob. The delay time can also be controlled with external trigger signals.
keywords: Two operating modes: Rec/Play and Play Only
Overdub capability in Rec/Play mode (with max feedback)
Playback via pedal or external trigger signal
Pitch change of sample sound during playback (via Time knob)
Digital delay function with 50 to 800 ms delay time
Delay time adjustable via S-mode (50-200ms) or L-mode (200-800ms) and Time knob
Delay time controllable via external trigger signals
Power supply: 9V (battery or AC adapter PSA-series)

name: FBM-1 Fender Bassman-Pedal
description: This pedal offers an incredibly precise digital recreation of the legendary 1959 Fender Bassman in sound, response, and character – including all controls, the bright input, the original logo, and a tweed-like finish. This is the only Fender-approved, authorized, and globally certified Bassman modeling pedal!
keywords: Recreates the unmistakable sound of the legendary 1959 Bassman
All control functions of the original amp
Original logo and cool vintage design
Controls: Pedal Switch, PRESENCE, MIDDLE, BASS, TREBLE, GAIN, LEVEL
Connections: IN, BRIGHT IN, OUT, AC Adapter
Power supply: DC 9 V (6F22/6LR61 battery or optional PSA-series AC adapter)

name: FT-2 Dynamic Filter
description: The FT-2 is equipped with a low-pass filter with adjustable slope (resonance). Unlike other wah effects, the FT-2 only influences the overtones of a sound, leaving the fundamental tone unchanged, ensuring excellent sound projection for any instrument, from guitar to keyboard to bass guitar. The FT-2 offers three operating modes: Up, Down, and Manual. In Up and Down modes, automatic upward or downward wah effects can be generated. By integrating BOSS's high-speed envelope circuit, the FT-2 can produce automatic wah effects faster and with higher accuracy than any conventional wah effect unit. The Manual mode allows the FT-2 to be used as a low-pass filter with adjustable cutoff frequency and resonance, or as a wah pedal by connecting the optional EV-5 expression pedal to the EXP input jack. When used as a wah pedal, the FT-2 never produces the scratching and popping noises associated with ordinary wah pedals. A Cutoff-Frequency control allows precise adjustment of the filter point, so the FT-2 can be adapted to any instrument. A "Q" control varies the wah effect over a wide range from subtle to extremely intense.
keywords: Affects only overtones, fundamental tone remains unchanged
Three operating modes: Up, Down, Manual
Manual low-pass filter function (adjustable cutoff frequency and resonance)
Wah pedal function with optional EV-5 expression pedal
No scratching or popping noises as a wah pedal
Power supply: 9V battery, AC adapter (ACA series)

name: GE-7 Graphic Equalizer
description: The GE-7 Graphic Equalizer is a small, compact equalizer designed for initial sound control at the instrument. The GE-7 also finds many applications as an effect unit, e.g., for boosting in a specific frequency range. The GE-7 has 7 octave bands with a control range of ±15dB per band and a center detent at 0dB. Since increasing the frequency also increases the volume, a 'Level' control was built in to adjust the overall volume back to the bypass level (signal without effect). Compared to other compact equalizers, the silent electronic switch allows the GE-7 to be switched on or off without 'cracking'. Another excellent feature is the signal-to-noise ratio of more than 90dB, which makes it quieter than many studio equalizers. The Graphic Equalizer GE-7 is a compact equalizer with all functions for extensive sound control of any musical signal. The GE-7 can be used for creative tonal shaping as well as compensating for deficiencies in room acoustics and/or the sound system. The GE-7 features seven octave ranges with a maximum boost or cut of ±15 dB per range, plus an overall effect level control. The extended frequency range of the GE-7 is sufficient for the fundamental and overtones of electric bass guitar, guitar, keyboards, and vocals. The maximum boost or cut of ±15 dB per octave band is sufficient for special effect applications and can be used even more effectively with the ±15 dB level control, which allows any desired balance between direct and effect signals to be set. The GE-7 is exceptionally quiet and features all the standard characteristics of BOSS compact pedals, such as silent FET switching, LED on/off and battery check indicator, non-slip feet, and easy access to the special battery compartment. It operates on a 9V battery with low current draw or an optional AC adapter.
keywords: Level control for overall volume adjustment (±15dB)
LED on/off and battery check indicator

name: GE-7 Graphic Equalizer
description: The GE-7 Graphic Equalizer is a small, compact equalizer designed for initial sound control on an instrument. It offers extensive tone control for any musical signal, from creative sound shaping to compensating for room acoustics or system deficiencies. It can also be used as an effect for boosting specific frequency ranges.
keywords: 7 octave bands with a control range of ±15dB per band and a center detent at 0dB
Built-in 'Level' control to adjust overall volume to match bypass level
Silent electronic switch for noise-free on/off operation
Extended frequency range suitable for fundamental and overtones of electric bass and guitar, keyboards, and vocals
Standard features of BOSS compact pedals including silent FET switching, LED on/off and battery check indicator, non-slip feet, and easy access to the battery compartment

name: LM-2 Limiter
description: The LM-2 Limiter addresses extreme transients and volume peaks in modern music, such as percussive synthesizer sounds or slapped bass/guitar. It prevents amplifier overload, recording device saturation, or even speaker damage by compressing volume peaks above an adjustable maximum. Utilizing a high-performance VCA, it guarantees an excellent signal-to-noise ratio without compromising sound quality.
keywords: High-performance VCA for excellent signal-to-noise ratio
Prevents overloading by compressing volume peaks
Threshold control sets the level at which limiting begins
Release control determines the decay time after the signal drops below the threshold
Power supply: 9V battery, AC adapter (ACA series)
Signal-to-noise ratio: -100 dB or less (IHF-A, Level and Tone controls at mid-position)

name: OD-2 Turbo-Overdrive
description: The Boss OD-2 'TURBO OverDrive' is a distortion effect for guitar, housed in the standard compact pedal enclosure used since 1977. Power is supplied either via an ACA power adapter or a 9V block battery. The OD-2 features a jack input and a jack output, along with three knobs and a rotary switch to engage the TURBO distortion, which shifts the sound from light distortion to medium-heavy and fatter tones. The knobs adjust Level, Tone, and Drive (distortion amount).
keywords: Powered by 9V battery or ACA power adapter
Features one jack input and one jack output
Three control knobs for Level, Tone, and Drive
Rotary switch to engage 'TURBO' distortion mode, offering light to medium-heavy and fatter tones

name: OD-2R Turbo Overdrive
description: The Boss OD-2R 'TURBO OverDrive' is a distortion effect for guitar in the compact pedal housing standardized since 1977. Power is supplied either via a PSA power adapter or a 9-V block battery. The OD-2R has a jack input, a jack output, and a REMOTE jack input, as well as three knobs and a rotary switch to activate the TURBO distortion, which shifts the sound from light distortion to medium-hard and fatter sounds. The knobs adjust Level, Tone, and Drive. The sound is similar to the OD-2; the difference is the ability to connect a footswitch to the REMOTE jack to switch the Turbo on and off.
keywords: Power via PSA adapter or 9V battery
Jack input, jack output, REMOTE jack input
Rotary switch for Turbo distortion (light, medium-hard, fat sounds)
Remote switch capability for Turbo on/off

name: PH-1 Phaser
description: Phase shift effects are among the most useful effects developed recently. The PH-1 produces phase shifts of up to 720°, creating all classic phase effects with clarity, brilliance, and depth. The two controls on the PH-1 are Speed and Depth. The speed control covers a wide LFO range from 100 ms to 16 seconds. The depth control regulates the effect intensity, allowing for the setting of any desired phasing effect. Combining all the above features with the technical 'BOSS Standard', the PH-1 is a uniquely flexible phaser suitable not only for guitar, bass, or keyboards but also ideally applicable in PA systems or studios due to its high signal-to-noise ratio.
keywords: Suitable for Guitar, Bass, Keyboards, PA, and Studio applications

name: PH-2 SUPER Phaser
description: From a 1986 Boss catalog: The compact PH-2 features 12-stage filter circuits and custom ICs for producing deep, naturally phase-shifted sounds comparable to those of larger and much more expensive phase shifters. On stage or in the studio, with guitars or keyboards, the PH-2 generates all the phase-shifted sounds you need. The PH-2 has two operating modes, selectable via a switch. In Mode I, the PH-2 produces deep, soft sounds suitable for guitar or keyboard accompaniment. By fully activating the 12-stage filter circuits, the PH-2 produces sharp sounds that enrich your performance with a distinctive touch. The PH-2 has three controls. The Rate knob adjusts the LFO speed. The effect depth is determined with the Depth knob. The Resonance knob intensifies the phase-shift effect by feeding the already phase-shifted signal back through the circuits.
keywords: 9V battery or ACA-series AC adapter power supply

name: PW-1 Rocker Wah
description: This Wah-Wah pedal features some innovations that cannot be overlooked. The effect width of the Wah-Wah is pre-adjustable with a knob, meaning the pedal travel always remains the same, only the Wah-Wah range changes. Switching between effect and bypass is done with a FET switch, as known from compact effects. The operating status is indicated by an LED, making the status visible even on a dark stage. This LED also serves as a battery check. The pedal naturally also has an AC adapter connection, volume adjustment, rubber feet, and a secure compartment for the battery. When we decided to develop real effect pedals, we faced a problem that many effect pedals had failed to solve: the controller for pedal control. Previously, normal potentiometers were used, but they started to crackle and scratch after a few hours of operation. These noises made the pedal unusable. Then optoelectronic control was invented, which is very sensitive to knocks and impacts. Often, the right replacement bulb(s) were missing at the crucial moment. To build a pedal like this Rocker Pedal free from any wear and tear, the invention of a new type of controller was necessary. With the new magnetic field controller, we achieved this optimum. This revolutionary controller design contains no touching mechanical parts and no sensitive or wear-prone elements. This controller works silently and cleanly for a lifetime.
keywords: LED status indicator (also for battery check)
Revolutionary magnetic field controller (wear-free, silent operation)

name: PW-10 V-Wah
description: The Wah Pedal for the 21st Century! This revolutionary, programmable modeling wah gives you immediate access to six characteristic classic and modern wah pedal sounds. Additionally, the legendary Uni-Vibe effect is included, as well as the completely new "Double Resonance" and "Voice" sounds that have never before been available in a wah pedal! Furthermore, the V-Wah offers eight simulations of legendary distortion pedals, three memory slots for custom sounds, and wear-free, noiseless infrared operation.
keywords: Six Classic and Modern Wah Models (CBY-Wah, VO-Wah, MO-Wah, Advanced, Bass, Custom)
Eight Overdrive/Distortion Types (e.g., OD-1, OD-2, MT-2, DS-1, BD-2, Muff Fuzz, Guv Dist, Booster)
New 'Voice' Mode for Talking Vocal Sounds
New 'Double Resonance' Mode for Analog Synth-like Sounds
Three Memory Slots for Custom Settings
Wear-free and Noiseless Infrared Pedal Mechanism
Wah Range Control for Filter Adjustment

name: RV-2 Digital Reverb
description: The RV-2, the first digital reverb in a foot pedal, offers the same professional sound quality typically found only in larger rack units. Its compact design makes the RV-2 particularly suitable for guitarists. With BOSS's developed DSP (Digital Signal Processing) technology in the RV-2's highly integrated components, it's possible to encapsulate the spatial ambiance of large halls down to small clubs in such a compact device. Six reverb modes - Room, two different Halls, Plate, Gated Reverb, and Panning Delay - are available for creating various effects. An adjustable reverb time of 0.2 - 10 seconds allows the player to choose the exact desired effect. A built-in pre-equalizer allows for suppressing lows and emphasizing highs to achieve a bright sound, or creating a rich, warm sound with deep bass and a dense mid-range. The RV-2 can produce the most popular reverb effects with superior sound quality and low noise. Stereo output jacks are provided, allowing you to enrich the reverb sounds with additional spatiality or take advantage of the panning effects in delay mode.
keywords: First digital reverb in a foot pedal
6 Reverb Modes: Room, Hall 1, Hall 2, Plate, Gated Reverb, Panning Delay
Power supply: 9V battery or AC adapter (PSA series)
Frequency response (direct): 10 Hz to 30 kHz ±1 dB
Frequency response (effect): 30 Hz to 10 kHz +1 dB, -3 dB

name: SG-1 Slow Gear
description: The BOSS Slow Gear is an effect unit that can give an instrument a special volume envelope. This makes it possible to give each note a violin-like attack. Previously, this effect was only possible by skillfully operating a volume pedal. The Slow Gear produces this volume envelope automatically and dynamically sensitive to touch. The Attack time is adjustable, variable between 50 and 300 ms; the second knob 'Sens' determines the effectiveness of the effect. The Slow Gear produces no unwanted sound changes and allows the guitarist or bassist to concentrate on their instrument and the music, without having to forgo this great effect.
keywords: Effect unit for special volume envelopes
Creates violin-like attack for each note
Automatic and touch-sensitive volume envelope generation

name: TU-120 Tuner
description: The TU-120 is a chromatic tuner with a rotary switch for the 12 fundamental tones and an LED chain to indicate tuning accuracy. The display range covers C2 to B6, with the concert pitch adjustable to 440, 442, 443, or 444 Hz. The light-emitting diodes (LEDs) form a kind of interference 'running light,' meaning they flash with varying brightness. When the brightest illumination remains in the same position, the tuning is correct; otherwise, the brightness maximum 'runs' to the right or left, depending on whether the string is tuned too high or too low. A built-in microphone allows tuning of acoustic instruments. Before tuning, the tuner must be calibrated by setting the FUNCTION switch to CHECK and turning the CALIBRATION knob until the brightest light stops in the center. Afterward, switch to TUNE to begin tuning. You can also switch to TONE mode to output the concert pitch. The TU-120 can be powered by a 9V block battery or an ACA AC adapter.
keywords: LED chain for tuning accuracy display (interference running light)
Concert pitch adjustable to 440, 442, 443, or 444 Hz
9V block battery or ACA AC adapter power

name: TU-12P Chromatic Tuner
description: The TU-12P is a chromatic tuner with a built-in microphone and pickup, allowing electric guitars to be tuned without a cable connection. It features a liquid crystal display with a bar graph and a tuning range from C1 to B5 with an adjustable reference pitch from 440 to 444 Hz.
keywords: Built-in pickup for cable-free tuning of electric guitars
Liquid crystal display (LCD) with bar graph

name: TU-2 Tuner
description: The TU-2 is a chromatic tuner in a compact pedal enclosure. The tuning range extends from C0 to C8 with an adjustable reference pitch from 438 to 445 Hz. Tuning accuracy is displayed via LEDs, and the fundamental note is shown on a 7-segment display. No microphone is built in for tuning acoustic instruments, but the TU-2 can, if a PSA power supply is connected, power other compact pedals.
keywords: Can power other compact pedals (with PSA power supply)

name: TU-50 Digital Tuner
description: The TU-50 is a chromatic tuner with a large LED display for fundamental notes and tuning accuracy, which is easily readable from a distance due to its half 19-inch width. The TU-50 belongs to the BOSS Pro series and has a tuning range from B0 to B7 with an adjustable reference pitch from 438 to 444 Hz. No microphone is built-in. The TU-50 functions as a level meter when the tuner function is inactive.
keywords: Large LED display for notes and tuning accuracy
Functions as a level meter when inactive

name: TU-60 Tuner
description: The TU-60 is a guitar tuner with a rotary switch for selecting the 6 strings, a built-in microphone for acoustic guitars, and 8 LEDs to indicate correct tuning. The 8 LEDs form a kind of 'interference running light,' meaning they flash with varying brightness. When the brightest illumination remains in the same position, the tuning is correct; otherwise, the brightness maximum 'runs' to the right or left, depending on whether the string is tuned too high or too low. The concert pitch is adjustable between 440 and 445 Hz. The TU-60 can only be operated with a 9V block battery. Before tuning, the tuner must be calibrated by setting the switch from OFF to CHECK and turning the CALIBRATION knob until the brightest light stays in the center. Then, switch to TUNER and begin tuning.
keywords: 8 LEDs with 'interference running light' for tuning indication
Concert pitch adjustable between 440 and 445 Hz

name: TU-8
description: The TU-8 is a guitar/bass tuner with a needle meter for precise tuning indication and LEDs for string status. In addition to standard tuning, the TU-8 supports open tunings (D, E, G, A major) or guitar tunings 1 or 2 semitones lower than normal. The tuning range extends from A0 to C8, with an adjustable reference pitch from 438 to 445 Hz. A built-in microphone allows tuning of acoustic guitars.
keywords: Supports Open Tunings (D, E, G, A major)
Supports guitar tunings 1 or 2 semitones lower
Powered by 1 x 9V block battery or PSA adapter

name: VB-2 Vibrato
description: The VB-2 Vibrato pedal adds a freely adjustable vibrato effect to any instrument, including electric pianos.  The delay time to reach the maximum vibrato amplitude is variable up to 4ms, creating a realistic vibrato.

name: 182 System 100M, Analog Sequencer
description: The Module 182 of the System-100M is a 2-channel, 8-step analog sequencer. The 2 channels can be operated in parallel or in series, providing a maximum of 16 steps. Continuous repetition or single pass-through is possible with the 'Repeat/Single' switch, and the number of steps can also be shortened to values smaller than 8 or 16. The speed can be controlled by a rotary knob or externally with a control voltage. Additionally, the steps can be advanced externally with a trigger signal. These diverse control options allow for the creation of very complex rhythmic patterns. The Module 182 is also Roland's last sequencer where steps can be individually adjusted directly via knobs. Simultaneously, the CSQ-100 was available, whose steps could be entered or played in via a CV/Gate keyboard. Furthermore, sequencers like the MC-8 or later MC-4 existed, whose steps could be programmed.

name: A-90 88-Key Master Keyboard
description: MIDI master keyboard with 88 weighted keys, PA-4 hammer action, adjustable velocity sensitivity, and channel aftertouch. 8 zones (4 internal and 4 external) can be assigned to 4 independent MIDI outputs, and 2 footswitches as well as 2 expression pedals can be connected. It features a performance memory with 64 slots and sequencer remote control (Song Select, Tempo, Reset, Start/Stop). A voice expansion board can be installed, transforming the A-90 from a pure master keyboard into an RD-Piano or JV-Synthesizer. The A-90 was also sold as the A-90EX with a pre-installed VE-RD1 board.
keywords: Sequencer remote control (Song Select, Tempo, Reset, Start/Stop)
Slot for Voice Expansion Board (can become RD-Piano or JV-Synthesizer)

name: A-90 88-Tasten Masterkeyboard
description: The Roland A-90 is a versatile MIDI master keyboard with 88 weighted keys, PA-4 hammer action, adjustable velocity sensitivity, and channel aftertouch. It features 8 zones (4 internal and 4 external) assignable to 4 independent MIDI outputs, along with connections for footswitches and expression pedals. It includes performance memory and sequencer remote control, and can be expanded with voice boards to function as an RD-Piano or JV-Synthesizer.

name: AD-50 'Double Beat' Fuzz-Wah Combi-Pedal
description: The Roland AD-50 'DOUBLE BEAT' is a floor effect pedal for guitar housed in a sturdy, black die-cast casing. It combines the AW-10 Wah pedal with a FUZZ effect. The Wah effect can be switched on or off by fully pressing the pedal. Located on the widened base next to the pedal are the controls for the Fuzz: a switch for FUZZ/NORMAL, a tone rotary switch with Sine, Square, and Peaks positions, an OUT LEVEL knob, and a SUSTAIN knob. The 'INSTRUMENT' jack input is on the left side (unlike most other Roland effects), and the mono jack output is on the right, which makes connecting multiple effects more difficult. The battery can be changed by opening the battery compartment cover, which is secured with two knurled screws on the underside. There is no power adapter connection. The AD-50 was manufactured by the Roland Music Engineering Group (Roland MEG), which was later renamed 'Boss'.
keywords: Fuzz controls: FUZZ/NORMAL switch, Tone rotary switch (Sine, Square, Peaks), OUT LEVEL, SUSTAIN

name: AS-1 Sustainer Pedal
description: The Roland AS-1 'Sustainer' is a floor effect pedal for guitar in a sturdy die-cast enclosure. This sustainer is used to lengthen played notes and has two controls, SUSTAIN and OUT LEVEL, and an on/off switch on the top. SUSTAIN controls the length of the sustain, OUT LEVEL controls the output level. The input jack (6.3mm mono jack), labeled INSTRUMENT, is on the right side, while the mono output jack 'OUTPUT' is on the left. The AS-1 features a clean sound and, unlike some other compressors, minimally alters the tone. The housing shape is the same as later used for (Roland) AF-60, AP-2, and (Boss) BF-1. To change the battery, the housing must be unscrewed from the bottom; mains operation is not provided. The AS-1 is Roland's first effect unit and was manufactured by the Roland Music Engineering Group (Roland MEG), which was later renamed 'Boss'.
keywords: Two controls: SUSTAIN and OUT LEVEL

name: AT-4 Acoustic Trigger Interface for TD-7
description: The AT-4 is a four-channel microphone preamplifier that boosts signals from 4 drum-mounted trigger microphones to the minimum level required by TD modules. However, the AT-4 does not guarantee that a trigger microphone will work with any TD module (SPD, HPD-15, etc.).
keywords: AT-4 Acoustic Trigger Interface for TD-7
Boosts signals from 4 drum-mounted trigger microphones to TD module required level

name: BW-1E Ballade für Windows
description: Sequencer Software

name: Backbeat MSD-BSD-04
description: Style disk for E-66/86/96, G800/RA95.  'Universal 4' style disk.

name: Boss CE-3 Chorus
description: The CE-3 Chorus combines the chorus effect of the popular CE-2 with stereo separation and other features.  It can create a stereo effect from a mono signal using outputs A and B.  Output A combines direct and effect signals in positive phase, while B uses negative phase.  It offers two modes: Mode 1 for true stereo chorus and Mode 2 where output B carries the unaltered signal.

name: Boss CS-1 Compression Sustainer
description: The CS-1 is a compressor unit that provides clean and undistorted sustain.  It features controls for volume, sustain time, and a Normal/Treble boost switch. The sustain control determines the compression level, while the switch allows emphasis on higher frequencies.

name: Boss DM-1 Delay Machine
description: The DM-1 is a compact, footswitchable echo unit offering a continuously variable delay time from 25 to 500 ms.  The intensity control allows variation from simple echoes to multiple echoes, and the balance control enables seamless mixing of direct and delay signals. Separate outputs enable the creation of a stereo effect when used with two amplifiers. Input sensitivity is adjusted via an input level switch for microphone, guitar, keyboard, or mixer input. An LED indicates overload.

name: Boss FT-2 Dynamic Filter
description: The FT-2 is a dynamic filter with adjustable resonance. Unlike other wah effects, it only affects the overtones, leaving the fundamental tone unchanged. It has three modes: Up, Down, and Manual, allowing for automatic or manual wah effects.  It can also function as a low-pass filter. An optional EV-5 expression pedal can be used for wah operation.

name: Boss PH-1
description: The PH-1 produces phase shifts up to 720° and thus creates all classic phase effects with clarity, brilliance and depth. The two controls on the PH-1 are speed and depth. The speed control covers a wide LFO range from 100 ms to 16 seconds. The depth control regulates the effect range and allows the setting of any desired phasing effect. Combining all the above-mentioned features with the technical "BOSS Standard", the PH-1 is a uniquely flexible phaser that is not only suitable for guitar, bass or keyboards, but also ideal for use in PA or studio applications due to its high noise voltage level.

name: Boss PH-2 Super Phaser
description: The compact PH-2 features 12-stage filter circuits and custom ICs to produce deep, naturally phase-shifted sounds comparable to those of larger and much more expensive phase shifters. On stage or in the studio, with guitars or keyboards, the PH-2 produces all the phase-shifted sounds you need. The PH-2 has two operating modes, which are selected via a switch. In Mode I, the PH-2 produces deep, soft sounds suitable for guitar or keyboard accompaniment. By fully activating the 12-stage filter circuits, the PH-2 produces sharp sounds that add a distinctive touch to your performance. The PH-2 has three controls. The Rate control sets the LFO speed. The effect depth is determined with the Depth control. The Resonance control intensifies the phase-shift effect by feeding back the already phase-shifted signal through the circuits.

name: CR-1000 DIGITAL DRUMMER
description: The Roland CR-1000 Digital Drummer is a flat, digital rhythm machine with 24 fixed rhythms and MIDI. The rhythm patterns are grouped into 3 selectable groups of 8 patterns each, also selectable via buttons. Each rhythm offers a variation, 4 fills, an intro, and an ending, each adjustable via illuminated buttons. Another button is used to add handclaps (electronic handclaps, a very popular sound in the 80s). Two larger buttons are for starting/stopping and manually triggering the fill-in. At the rear edge of the control surface are eight mini-knobs and a 3-character display, which usually shows the tempo. One of the knobs (ACCENT) is for the strength of the accentuation, another for the groove, adjustable from straight to heavily shuffled. The remaining knobs control the volumes of 1. Bass drum, 2. Snare/Rim/Clap, 3. Timbale/Toms, 4. Cymbals/Hi-hat, 5. Conga, 6. Claves/Cowbell. The tempo can be set with a large rotary knob from 28 to 249 BPM or via external MIDI clock synchronization. Next to it is the smaller volume knob. On the rear are three button connections for START/STOP, FILL-IN, RESTART, the mono output, MIDI IN and MIDI THRU, the power supply jack, and the on/off switch. The CR-1000 can be operated with a power supply unit or with 6 AA batteries.
keywords: Variation, 4 fills, intro, and ending per rhythm
Separate Volume controls for Bassdrum, Snare/Rim/Clap, Timbale/Toms, Cymbals/Hihat, Conga, Claves/Cowbell
External pedal inputs for Start/Stop, Fill-In, Restart

name: CSQ-600 Digital Sequencer, 600 Steps for CV/Gate
description: The CSQ-600 is a digitally controlled sequencer for analog CV/Gate signals. It offers 4 sequences, each with a maximum of 150 steps (notes), which are retained even after power-off thanks to the built-in battery. The four sequences can be combined in any order. Separate recording of CV and control time in two passes is possible, as is external (slave) synchronization of the CSQ-600. Recorded sequences are retained by a battery for a period after being switched off; there is no option to save the sequences permanently.

name: D-5 LA Synthesizer
description: The D-5 is a 9-part multitimbral, 32-voice digital synthesizer with 61 velocity-sensitive synthesizer keys, an arpeggiator, and MIDI. 8 tonally playable parts and a rhythm part use LA synthesis, a combination of 2 tones via one of 13 structures. A tone consists either of a PCM oscillator (ROM samples) with a subsequent amp, or a simple oscillator (triangle/square/...) with a dynamic filter and amp. The samples are slightly shorter than those in the D-50. The sound generation is the same as in the D-10, D-20, and D-110. A PG-10 programmer can be connected for programming. Compared to the D-10, it also differs by having a slightly lower-quality keyboard, a different user interface, an external power supply, and an additional arpeggiator.

name: DA-400 Digital-Analog Converter, 4-channel for S-760
description: The DA-400 is a 4-channel Digital/Analog Converter in a 9.5" format. It features 2 digital S/P-DIF inputs (one switchable between optical and coaxial, the other coaxial only) and 4 jack outputs.

name: DB-770 Digital Booster
description: The DB-770 is a 9.5-inch device that has a coaxial S/P-DIF input and output, between which a digital audio signal can be boosted by +3, +6, or +x dB. The DB-770 has no other functions.

name: DJ-70 Disco Stereo Sampler Workstation
description: The stereo sampler DJ-70 features a velocity-sensitive 3-octave keyboard, is 24-voice polyphonic, 31-part multitimbral, and includes an 8-track sequencer with RPS. The sampler unit uses the same data format as the S-700 series, layering up to 4 samples in partials, of which up to 88 form a patch. Each partial includes dynamic amplifiers and filters with resonance. The DJ-70 can reload samples during playback and also process sound floppy disks from the S-330 and S-550. The DJ-70 comes with 2MB of sample memory, which can be upgraded to 4MB. The only storage medium used is the floppy disk drive (DD and HD floppies). A special feature is the Scratch-Dial, which allows samples to be scratched like records.

name: Edirol R-09
description: The Edirol R-09 is a 2-channel WAVE/MP3 recorder.  It records at 24-bit resolution at either 44.1 kHz or 48 kHz onto an SD card (supports 64MB to 2GB SD cards, and 4GB to 8GB SDHC cards). It has a built-in stereo microphone, but can also record from external microphones or line inputs. Data is transferred to a computer via Mini-USB; the recorder appears as a mass storage device.

name: FA-76 Fantom
description: The Fantom (FA-76) is a digital synthesizer workstation with 76 velocity-sensitive synthesizer keys, a sequencer, and a flexible arpeggiator. The sound generation is 16-part multitimbral and based on the XV sound engine, which forms patches from up to four tones. Each tone consists of a stereo PCM oscillator, dynamic filter and amp, 3 envelopes, and LFOs. Two tones can be linked by one of 10 structures. All parameters are fully editable. In addition to programmable patterns, the arpeggiator includes a rhythm section and many complex preset arpeggio/rhythm patterns. The sequencer offers 16 tracks, each capable of recording all 16 MIDI channels, 100 patterns, tempo and time signature tracks, and can hold one song in memory, as well as play songs directly from a 3.5' HD floppy disk. Although the FA-76 already carries the 'Fantom' name, it cannot use its own samples as the basis for the oscillators. This original Fantom still belongs to the XV series. Additional key points include 1024 patches (640 preset, 128 user, 256 GM2 sounds) plus 29 rhythm sets, a variable arpeggiator and rhythm generator with real-time control via rotary knobs, buttons, and D-Beam infrared controller, a high-resolution sequencer with Realtime Phrase Sequencing (RPS function), 24-bit Reverb plus Chorus and 90 multi-effects such as COSM Amp Modeling, expandability with one SR-JV80 and two SRX Wave Expansion Boards, 24-bit D/A converters and S/PDIF digital outputs, and a floppy drive for saving user data.

name: G-303 Guitar for GR-300
description: The G-303 is a controller guitar for Roland guitar synthesizers with a 24-pin connector, featuring a distinctive double-cutaway shape. In addition to the 24-pin connector for the special 'hexaphonic' pickup's signal (which outputs individual string signals to control GR synthesizers), the guitar also has a standard guitar output for the sound of its two built-in humbucker pickups. This means the G-303 can also be used as a regular guitar. All metal parts are nickel-plated; the body is mahogany, and the glued-in neck is maple. The G-303 differs from the simultaneously available G-808 only by its glued-in rather than neck-through construction and the wood used. The G-303 was manufactured by Ibanez/Greco (specifically by supplier Fuji Gen Gakki) according to Roland's specifications. Sound control is provided by four gold (plastic) knobs for Master Volume, Guitar Tone, Cutoff Frequency, and Balance between guitar and synthesizer levels, two black knobs for Resonance (VCF) and Vibrato intensity, a three-stage mode switch, and another three-stage switch between guitar and synthesizer signals or both. The G-303 is the legendary guitar played by Pat Metheny, as well as Andy Summers (The Police), Adrian Belew, and Robert Fripp (King Crimson). The G-303 was also available in white (G-303W) and as a left-handed model (G-303LH).
keywords: Controller guitar for Roland guitar synthesizers
Controls for Master Volume, Guitar Tone, Cutoff Frequency, Guitar/Synthesizer balance
Controls for Resonance (VCF) and Vibrato intensity
Three-stage switch for guitar/synthesizer signal or both

name: G-77FL Bass Guitar for GR-77 B (Fretless)
description: The G-77FL is a fretless controller bass for Roland Bass Synthesizers with a 24-pin connection. It features a very distinctive "handle" design, a fiberglass stabilizer intended to prevent unwanted neck vibrations. In addition to the 24-pin connector for the signal of the special individual-string pickup used to control GR synthesizers (GR-33B or GR-77B), the bass also has a normal bass output that outputs the sound of its two standard pickups. The G-77FL can therefore also be used as a regular bass, although its shape may cause it to slip when played sitting down. Besides the fiberglass stabilizer, the bass is made of alder and maple. Sound control is provided by a larger (plastic) Master Volume knob and six smaller black knobs for Pickup Balance (between the two normal pickups), Guitar Tone, and Balance (between normal bass and bass synthesizer), Cutoff, Resonance (VCF) or EDIT, and Vibrato Intensity. Below these is a three-stage mode switch, which has different functions depending on the connected synthesizers. The G-77FL was also available with frets as the G-77.
keywords: G-77FL Bass Guitar for GR-77 B (Fretless)

name: GI-20 GK-to-MIDI Interface
description: The Roland GI-20 is a Guitar/Bass-To-MIDI interface for guitars or basses with a 13-pin connector and GK-Pickup (GK-2, GK-3, GK-2B, GK-3B, etc.) in a 9.5-inch housing (half-width, 1U 19-inch rack compatible). A switch on the back determines whether the GI-20 expects GK signals from a bass or a guitar. A GK-Pickup is required in any case. Global settings allow saving four sensitivity settings for how the GI-20 reacts to individual strings. Further settings can be stored in 50 patch memories for complex assignments at once. Per string, the pitch can be transposed from -36 to +24 semitones, the bend range can be adjusted, and it can be determined whether the string outputs data at all. MIDI base channel, poly or mono mode, 6 fingerpicking modes, and controller assignments (rear-connectable expression pedal, footswitches 1 and 2, Volume, and S1/S2 buttons on the GK-Pickup) are also stored per patch. A tuner is built-in, with its reference pitch adjustable from 427.6 Hz to 452.8 Hz in 0.2 Hz steps. Via a Bulk Dump (memory transfer), all patch settings can be output together as SysEx data via MIDI OUT, recorded with an external sequencer, and later reloaded via MIDI IN. Additionally, a USB-MIDI interface for Windows 98/Me/2000/XP and Mac OS 8.5 to 9 is built-in, which can be used instead of the MIDI jacks, allowing direct input into a similarly equipped computer. The Guitar-to-MIDI conversion is fast, even faster than the GI-10, but still has noticeable latency, especially for low notes.
keywords: 13-pin connector for GK-Pickup (GK-2, GK-3, GK-2B, GK-3B required)

name: GK-2B Pickup System for V-Bass
description: The Roland GK-2B is a hexaphonic pickup with a 13-pin connector for mounting on a standard bass, designed to control 13-pin bass synthesizers or virtual bass systems. Unlike normal pickups, a hexaphonic pickup captures each string individually, providing 4 to 6 separate signals depending on the number of strings on the bass. The GK-2B is essentially two parts: the pickup itself, which should be mounted about 10mm behind the bridge, and a small control unit connected via a short cable, containing the controls. The control unit, fixed to the strap button and bass surface with a special bracket, has a mini-jack input to connect the signal from the normal pickups, allowing it to also be transmitted via the 13-pin cable. The control unit features two buttons "Up/S2" and "Down/S1", a control for (synth) volume, a switch for BASS to MIX to pure GK signal, and the 13-pin connector for the GK cable. The GK-2B is not a MIDI pickup, as often incorrectly stated, but rather the prerequisite for a 13-pin device (e.g., V-Bass, GR-20, GI-20, VB-99, etc.) to convert its signals into MIDI.
keywords: Two-part design: pickup and control unit
Control unit with mini-jack input for normal bass pickups
Switch for BASS / MIX / pure GK signal

name: GKP-4
description: The Roland GKP-4, labeled 'GK Parallel Box', is a quadruple distributor for the GK signal of a guitar to four 13-pin devices, such as GR synthesizers (GR-09, GR-1, GR-20, GR-30, GR-33, GR-50), Guitar-to-MIDI interfaces (GI-10, GI-20), Virtual Guitar Systems (VG-8, VG-88, VG-99) and other GK devices (OC-20G, WP-20G). On the front side of the elongated bar is the 13-pin input, the four outputs are arranged next to each other on one side, and two sets of four associated switches are on the opposite side. With these switches, you can individually determine for each output A to D whether the control signals 'S1/Down' and 'S2/Up' from the GK pickup are output (ON) or not (OFF). The other switch determines whether the synthesizer volume setting from the GK-2 should be passed to the respective output (ON) or not (OFF). The GKP-4 is powered via the GK device connected to output A.

Individual switches for GK-2 synthesizer volume setting per output
Powered via connected GK device (output A)

name: GR-09 Guitar Synthesizer
description: The Roland GR-09 Guitar Synthesizer is an affordable and intuitive instrument that brings Roland's powerful synthesizer technology to guitarists. It allows users to incorporate the latest digital sounds into their music without altering their playing technique, suitable for professionals, semi-pros, and hobbyists alike.

name: GR-100 Guitar Synthesizer
description: The Roland GR-100 is an electronic effects unit for guitars with a 24-pin connection. Unlike the Roland GR-300, which is a true guitar synthesizer, the GR-100 is essentially a hexaphonic fuzz box with a subsequent filter and a chorus. Roland wisely called the GR-100 "Electronic Guitar" instead of "Guitar Synthesizer". Three built-in footswitches are used to turn the chorus or filter modulation on/off and to invert the filter envelope. Filter modulation can be adjusted with controls for Peak and Sensitivity (Sens), one control determines Chorus intensity (Sens), and another controls the Vibrato rate (intensity is controlled by a knob on the G-Guitar). There are no more controls, but there is a 24-pin connector on the top and, on the rear, connections for a VCF control pedal and three audio outputs: Chorus, Mix, and Guitar, as well as the power switch.
keywords: Three built-in footswitches for Chorus On/Off, Filter Modulation On/Off, Filter Envelope Inversion
Controls for Peak and Sensitivity (Filter Modulation)
Three audio outputs: Chorus, Mix, Guitar
Included accessories: C-24D 24-pin cable, PJ-1 audio cable

name: GR-300 Guitar Synthesizer
description: The GR-300 is a 6-voice polyphonic analog synthesizer designed for 24-pin guitar control systems. Each string controls one of the six VCOs, which can also be individually switched off via 6 String Select switches if needed. A globally switchable compressor significantly extends sustain. For two integrated footswitches (A and B), a pitch deviation and a common rise and fall time can be set, defining how quickly the deviation is reached or released. Two switches above them determine whether the deviation is applied only while a footswitch is pressed or alternately with each press. For the subsequent filter, the attack time and the sensitivity of the filter envelope to the strike can be adjusted, or switched off with an integrated footswitch if necessary. Another footswitch can invert the envelope. Cutoff frequency and resonance are adjusted with the guitar's controls. The intensity of LFO pitch modulation is also controlled from the guitar, with a rate knob available on the GR-300 itself. Vibrato is activated by pressing the 'Touch-Plate' sensors next to the guitar pickup. DUET is the fifth footswitch, which activates a chorus effect. On the rear, there are connections for a pedal to control the cutoff frequency, buttons for the compressor, sweep trigger, and string select, the 24-pin connector, and audio outputs MIX/SYNTH and GUITAR. If GUITAR output is used, the pure guitar signal is sent there and no longer routed to the shared MIX output. The GR-300 responds very quickly to the controlling guitar and can be controlled by G-202, G-303, G-707, G-808, and a mounted GK-1. The first control guitar, GS-500, is not suitable.
keywords: Each string controls an individual VCO (6 VCOs total)

name: GR-500
description: The Roland GR-500 is a polyphonic, analog guitar synthesizer with a 24-pin connection, which can only be controlled with the special GS-500 guitar. On the slanted surface of the box-shaped housing (similar to the Synthesizer Expander 102), the controls are divided into the five sections of the GR-500. To the far left are the common threshold control for the synthesizer's response sensitivity, the phones jack for headphones, the master volume control (Level), and the on/off switch. The first section (G) is for the pure guitar signal, which can only be tapped at the GR-500, not the guitar. A tone control (named EQ Freq), the on/off switch for the EQ, and an output selector switch are the only controls in this section. The GR-500 has three output sum buses, so for each section, you can choose with a switch which sum the signal is routed to. On the back, there are three outputs (CH1 to CH3) and a MIX output, where all three sums are present together. The subsequent section P is called POLYENSEMBLE and converts the signals of all 6 guitar strings into synthesizer signals of the same pitch but without following dynamics. For this, there are sliders for Attack, Decay, and Sustain, which shape the envelope. With appropriate settings, a note struck once on the guitar can sound for up to 5 minutes. The sound of this section can be adjusted with four sliders: F (fundamental = volume of the fundamental tone), L (Low), M (Middle), and H (High) for the low, mid, and high overtones. The subsequent Bass section is monophonic with priority on the last played note. You can choose whether this section reacts to all strings, only the lowest three, or the lowest two strings. The sound is mixed by three sliders: Percussion, Soft, and Hard, with this section being velocity-sensitive and operating in the 16-foot range. Here, too, three envelope sliders are present, with an additional switch to toggle the release time between Short and Long. The main section called SOLO corresponds to a classic, monophonic synthesizer with priority on the last note: VCO with 8-foot sawtooth, 8 and 16-foot square waves with pulse width modulation are mixed and sent through a low-pass filter (VCF, 24dB/Oct) followed by a VCA. The filter can be modulated by LFO, the envelope, and velocity. The control section for an external synthesizer concludes, featuring Portamento and Transpose controls and providing control signals on the rear as CV/Gate signals. The on/off states and volumes for the individual sections are controlled via the corresponding controls of the GS-500 control guitar. The GR-500 is the very first guitar synthesizer and requires a certain degree of playing accuracy and practice to achieve satisfactory results.

name: JS-30 Sampling Workstation
description: A new type of sampler for today's music. Phrase sampling is an indispensable part of dance and pop music production today. Now Roland introduces the JS-30 Sampling Workstation: A high-quality phrase sampling instrument for every musician and DJ at a very attractive price. With its thoughtful design and truly simple operation, even complex phrase sampling becomes child's play. You don't even have to be able to play an instrument. These features make the JS-30 the ideal instrument for club DJs, professional studios, and home studios. It opens up completely new, practically limitless possibilities for music creation. With a single JS-30, you immediately become a remix artist, no prior experience with musical instruments is necessary. Simply combine phrases as you like and compose new songs this way. This is how music is made today! The JS-30 was specifically developed for phrase sampling. It has a clear and logically structured control panel for the simplest real-time handling, distinguishing it pleasantly from conventional rackmount samplers. There is a dedicated button for each function, making it as easy as possible. The perfect sampler: The design of the JS-30 Sampling Workstation builds on Roland's extensive experience in building digital samplers. The excellent sound results from the use of sampler chips, which were already used in the Roland S-770 and S-760 digital samplers. The JS-30 offers practically the same sound quality as the S-series samplers with 16-bit sampling at 44.1kHz. Record, play, and mix "off the cuff": All you have to do to record samples is connect a CD player, a tape recorder, or a microphone and press the Start/Stop button. That's all! The sample is automatically assigned to one of the 12 keypads and is ready for playback. You don't have to worry about presets or assignments at all. In case you do want to intervene yourself, the JS-30 offers extensive editing options including Truncate and Loop. Double sample time: The internal memory has a sample time of 22.5 seconds at a sampling rate of 44.1kHz. With the useful Time x 2 function, the time can be extended to 45 seconds. By installing additional SIMMs, the sample time can be extended to a full 45 seconds (90 seconds with the Time x 2 function). Even more possibilities through the built-in SCSI port: The JS-30 has a SCSI port, so you can connect powerful data storage devices such as hard drives or MO (Magnetic Optical) drives. This gives you practically unlimited storage space. You can simply save your phrases and load them back for playback. In addition, a CD-ROM player can be connected to the SCSI port. The JS-30 is able to read CD-ROMs for the Roland S-Series samplers, so you can also use the huge CD-ROM libraries with first-class stereo samples. Versatile functions for music productions: Sample BPM setting: The tempo of a sample phrase can be easily set by entering the BPM (Beats Per Minute) value with the Ten Key Pad. If you don't know the exact value, you can also use the practical Tap-Tempo function. Master BPM: It is child's play to align different sample phrases with different tempos to form a chain: set the Master BPM value with the Ten Key Pad, and the sample phrases will automatically adjust to the tempo you specify. The original BPM values are retained for later use.

The JV-1000 has a slot for a Voice Expansion Board, allowing it to be expanded by 28 voices with specialized (GM or JV-80) sounds. The sound generation of the JV-1000 is identical to that of the JV-90, and a patch (sound program) consists of up to 4 Tones, two of which can be combined via one of 10 structures. A Tone consists of a PCM oscillator, 12dB multi-mode filter, dynamic amplifier, 3 envelopes, and 2 LFOs. Depending on the chosen structure, a booster and ring modulator can optionally be added, and with identical settings for two filters, a quality of 24dB can be achieved. Since Tones can be limited by velocity and note range, split, layer, and crossover sounds are possible within a single patch. The combination of up to 7 parts (with patches) and a rhythm set is managed by a Performance. The JV-1000's sound library can be expanded with a Wave Expansion Board and/or an SO-PCM1 card, providing additional PCM samples to the oscillators. The JV-1000 has a built-in 8-track sequencer with a floppy disk drive and a second display (!), which corresponds to the functionality of the MC-50. 8 internal songs are available, and each track can record data from all 16 MIDI channels. 1 tempo track and a pattern-oriented rhythm track complete the sequencer.

name: MC-300 Micro Composer with 3.5" Floppy
description: The MC-300 is a song-oriented MIDI sequencer with 2 independent MIDI outputs and a 3.5" floppy drive, whose operating system must be loaded from a floppy disk at startup. The hardware largely corresponds to the MC-500 but features small, flat buttons instead of large, high-travel buttons. The MC-300 was shipped with MRC-300 software, which turns it into a 4-track sequencer, capable of recording all 16 MIDI channels on each track. Additionally, a rhythm track is available, allowing up to 90 rhythm patterns with up to 32 different note numbers each to be arranged. These patterns can also be created by the user. The MC-300 can hold up to 8 songs in memory, provided there is enough space. Using the Microscope function, all entries (events) can be fully edited. Unfortunately, for various functions, the system diskette must be re-inserted repeatedly, which can be somewhat annoying. However, the MC-300 can also be started with other operating systems available for the MC-500 and MC-500MKII. With the S-MRC (Super-MRC) software, the MC-300 becomes an 8-track sequencer, also with a pattern-oriented rhythm track, where up to 240 patterns can be created instead of 90. The Performance-Package MRP-500 allows for creating stage-ready MRC-300 song sequences, complete with pauses (or not) and repetitions, which can be started with a simple button press. The Rhythm Bank MRD-500 provides pre-programmed patterns and software for arranging rhythm tracks, and the Bulk Librarian MRB-500 enables the management of bulk dumps from various – including non-Roland – devices. Furthermore, the MRM-500 software was available, allowing MRC-500 and S-MRC songs to be converted to Standard MIDI Files (SMF) and vice-versa. Unlike the MC-500, the MC-300's memory cannot be expanded and holds a maximum of 25,000 events. The MC-300 can be synchronized internally or externally via MIDI Clock signals, as well as via an FSK signal (Tape Sync) to tape machines.
