MRB-500 Bulk Librarian for managing bulk dumps (including non-Roland devices)
Synchronization: internal, external MIDI Clock, FSK (Tape Sync)

name: MC-50 MIDI Sequencer
description: The MC-50 is a compact, song-oriented MIDI sequencer with 2 independent MIDI outputs, a 3.5" floppy drive, and a backlit display. Unlike its predecessors (MC-500/MKII), the main operating system does not need to be loaded from disk; the 8-track S-MRC sequencer and the Super-MRP Performance Package program are already integrated, making the MC-50 immediately ready for use. However, the MC-50 cannot directly process Standard MIDI Files (SMF) or bulk dumps from other devices, which is why it can be fed alternative operating systems from disk (MRB-500 Bulk Librarian or MRM-500 SMF-Converter). In normal operation, the MC-50 is an 8-track sequencer, with all 16 MIDI channels recordable on each track. Additionally, a rhythm track is available, on which up to 240 rhythm patterns with up to 32 different note numbers each can be arranged. These patterns can also be created by the user. The MC-50 can hold up to a maximum of 8 songs in memory, provided the memory space (approx. 40,000 events) is sufficient. With the Microscope function, all entries (events) can be fully edited. The MC-50 can be synchronized internally or externally via MIDI Clock signals, as well as via an FSK signal (tape sync) to tape machines. The MC-50 needs to convert floppy disks and songs from its predecessors MC-500, MC-300, and MC-500MKII and cannot play them directly. Reverse conversion of MC-50 songs to MC-300/500(MKII) songs is not possible.
keywords: Dedicated Rhythm Track (up to 240 patterns, 32 note numbers each)
Microscope Function for Full Event Editing
Internal or External MIDI Clock Synchronization
Includes ACI Power Supply, Floppy DD Memory, MSC MIDI Cable
Supports optional MF-2DD Disks and DP-2 Footswitch

name: MC-500 MIDI Micro-Composer with 3.5" Floppy Drive
description: The MC-500 is a song-oriented MIDI sequencer with 2 independent MIDI outputs and a 3.5-inch floppy drive, whose operating system must be loaded from a disk at startup. The hardware, with its numeric keypad and overall design, strongly resembles a calculator and feels excellent to operate. It features 6 drive buttons, 7 function buttons, 2 cursor buttons, an alpha-dial for value input, 5 illuminated track buttons, and an unfortunately non-backlit 2-line display for operation. Originally, the MC-500 shipped with MRC-500 software, turning it into a 4-track sequencer, where all 16 MIDI channels can be recorded on each track. Additionally, besides a tempo track, there's a rhythm track available, on which up to 90 rhythm patterns with up to 32 different note numbers each can be arranged. These patterns can also be created by the user. The MC-500 can hold up to 8 songs in memory, provided there is enough space. Using the 'Microscop' function, all entries (events) can be fully edited. Unfortunately, for various functions, the system diskette must be reinserted repeatedly, which can be somewhat annoying. However, the MC-500 can also be started with other operating systems. With the S-MRC (Super-MRC) software, the MC-500 becomes an 8-track sequencer, also with a pattern-oriented rhythm track, where 240 patterns are possible. The MRP-500 Performance Package allows the creation of stage-ready MRC-500 song sequences that can be started completely with pauses (or without) and repetitions by simple button press. The MRD-500 Rhythm Bank package provides pre-programmed patterns and software for arranging rhythm tracks, and the MRB-500 Bulk Librarian enables the management of bulk dumps from various – including non-Roland – devices. When the MC-500MKII was released, an OM-500 memory expansion became available, expanding the memory to the size of the MC-500MKII. There was also the MRM-500 software, which could convert MRC-500 and S-MRC songs to Standard MIDI Files (SMF) and vice-versa. The MC-500 with MRC-500 or S-MRC combines the advantages of all previous sequencers except analog step sequencers. The MC-500 holds a maximum of 25,000 events and can be synchronized internally or externally via MIDI Clock signals, as well as via an FSK signal (Tape Sync) to tape recorders.
keywords: MC-500 MIDI Micro-Composer with 3.5" Floppy Drive
6 drive buttons, 7 function buttons, 2 cursor buttons, alpha-dial, 5 illuminated track buttons
MRC-500 software (4-track sequencer, 16 MIDI channels per track)
Rhythm track (up to 90 rhythm patterns, each with up to 32 note numbers)
MRM-500 software for Standard MIDI File (SMF) conversion
Synchronizes via MIDI Clock or FSK (Tape Sync) with tape recorders

name: MC-505 Synthesizer-Groovebox
description: The MC-505 GrooveBox consists of an 8-part multitimbral digital synthesizer and a pattern sequencer. The sound generation principle is based on the 4-Tone-10Structure architecture of the JV/XP series, with the ROM samples replaced by dance-oriented sounds. The sequencer is pattern-oriented, with 8 tracks fixed to parts (and MIDI channels 1 to 7 and 10). During playback, tracks can be muted individually via buttons, and the MEGAMIX function allows exchanging tracks of the current pattern with those of other patterns. An arpeggiator and RPS sequencer can also be used alternatively.
keywords: Sound generation based on JV/XP series (4-Tone-10Structure architecture)
MEGAMIX function for pattern track exchange

name: MC-80 16 Track Hardware Sequencer
description: The MC-80 is a professional 16-track hardware MIDI sequencer with a large LCD, floppy disk drive, and expandable memory. It features a high-resolution sequencer, RPS (Realtime Phrase Sequencing) function, and a variety of advanced MIDI editing tools for complex musical arrangements. It can be expanded with a SCSI board and synthesizer boards.
keywords: Floppy disk drive for data storage
Expandable with synthesizer boards (e.g., VE-GS PRO)

name: MD-8 MIDI/DCB Interface for JUNO-60/JUPITER-8
description: The Roland MD-8 is a MIDI-DCB converter that connects Roland's 'Digital-Connection-Bus' equipped synthesizers, such as the Jupiter-8 and Juno-60, with the MIDI world. Only the MIDI channel is adjustable; program changes and notes are converted into DCB signals, and notes into MIDI data. Controller data is not converted.
keywords: Connects Jupiter-8 and Juno-60 to MIDI
Converts program changes and notes to DCB signals

name: MD-8 MIDI/DCB Interface für JUNO-60/JUPITER-8
description: The Roland MD-8 is a MIDI-DCB converter that connects Roland synthesizers equipped with the MIDI predecessor 'Digital-Connection-Bus', such as the Jupiter-8 and Juno-60, to the MIDI world. Only the MIDI channel is adjustable; program changes and notes are converted into DCB signals, and notes into MIDI data. Controller data is not converted.
keywords: Connects Jupiter-8 and Juno-60 (with Digital-Connection-Bus) to MIDI
Converts MIDI program changes and notes to DCB signals
Converts DCB notes to MIDI data

name: MKS-7 MIDI Soundmodul Super-Quartett
description: The MKS-7 SUPER QUARTET is a multitimbral, analog synthesizer module in a 19-inch, 2U rack format with PCM rhythm sounds. It features 4 sections: a monophonic BASS section with 20 sounds, a two-voice MELODY section, and a four-voice CHORD section, each with 100 sounds. The rhythm section, fixed to MIDI channel 10, offers 11 immutable drum sounds (PCM samples): BD, SN, HiT, MiT, LoT, CH, OH, Clap, Rim, Ride, Crash, which correspond to those of the TR-707. The note numbers are fixed. The sound generation of the three melodic sections is equivalent to that of the Juno-106, meaning each voice has a DCO (digitally controlled oscillator), high-pass filter, dynamic low-pass filter, dynamic amp, and one envelope. Editing sounds on the device itself is only possible in a special engineering mode; however, current sounds can be modified via MIDI SysEx data using, for example, a Juno-106 (editor) or HS-60. The MKS-7 is the first (more than 2-part) multitimbral MIDI synthesizer ever to include drum sounds. The MKS-7 can also be switched into a WHOLE mode, where only the CHORD part is active but becomes 6-voice, essentially a Juno-106 in rack format.
keywords: 4 sections: monophonic BASS (20 sounds), two-voice MELODY (100 sounds), four-voice CHORD (100 sounds)
Rhythm section (fixed to MIDI channel 10) with 11 immutable TR-707 drum sounds (PCM samples): BD, SN, HiT, MiT, LoT, CH, OH, Clap, Rim, Ride, Crash
Sound generation for melodic sections similar to Juno-106 (DCO, high-pass filter, dynamic low-pass filter, dynamic amp, one envelope per voice)
Sounds editable via MIDI SysEx (e.g., with Juno-106 or HS-60)
WHOLE mode for 6-voice CHORD section (Juno-106 in rack format)
Includes connection cables, 2 MSC MIDI cables

name: MM-4 MIDI THRU Box
description: The MM-4 is a MIDI distributor, or in modern terms: a MIDI THRU box. One MIDI input is routed to four parallel outputs. The MM-4 requires an external power supply (Boss PSA-230); battery operation or power from the MIDI data stream is not possible.
keywords: Cannot be powered via MIDI data stream

name: MO-7 Magnetic Optical Disc Laufwerk 600MB für S-770
description: The MO-7 is a magneto-optical storage drive with SCSI connections. It features the Sony 5.25-inch SMO-501 drive, which can also handle 650MB media, but Roland samplers require media with 512kB sectors, so the MO-7 "only" offers 600MB of storage space per MO disk. However, this 600MB is not available at once, as the media (MO disks) are double-sided and offer only 300MB per side. The SCSI ID is freely adjustable, and the MO-7 is not internally terminated. Both SCSI connections are implemented as 50-pin Centronics connectors.
keywords: MO-7 Magnetic Optical Disc Laufwerk 600MB für S-770
600MB storage per MO disk (300MB per side)
Requires 512kB sector media for Roland samplers

name: MPU-101 MIDI/CV-Interface
description: The MPU-101 is a MIDI-to-CV interface featuring CV, Dynamics, and Gate outputs for 4 channels, along with 4 additional control outputs. The MIDI receive channel can be freely configured. Depending on the polyphony setting, the remaining CV/Gate channels are supplied by the next higher MIDI channels. The MPU-101 can also be operated in Time-Code mode, where only the Gate outputs function, providing MIDI-clock-synchronous trigger pulses for quarter, eighth notes, and triplets. These pulses can be used to control older rhythm machines, arpeggiators of vintage synthesizers, or for synchronizing analog sequencers. The MPU-101 was initially announced as MI-10 but was never released under that designation.
keywords: Additional control outputs: Bender (-1 to +1V), Modulation (0 to +10V), Aftertouch (0 to +10V), Volume (0 to +10V)
Freely adjustable MIDI receive channel (1 to 16)
Time-Code mode for MIDI-clock-synchronous trigger pulses (quarter, eighth, triplets)
Built-in power supply with fixed power cable
LED indicators for Power, Gate (x4), Hold mode (x5)

name: MPU-104 MIDI Input Selector
description: The MIDI Input Selector MPU-104 is a switch that routes exactly one of 5 MIDI inputs to the output. Accordingly, on the back of the 1/2 19-inch housing, there are 5 MIDI IN and one MIDI THRU jack. Power supply via an external PSA power adapter is only necessary if, in addition to the visibly depressed switch, the LED above it should also light up. Switching is purely mechanical and does not protect against stuck notes, etc., if the switching time is chosen unfavorably. Since the MPU-104 switches mechanically, the function can also be reversed: as a splitter of one MIDI cable into 5 alternative routings. The MPU-104 was originally supposed to be called MI-40 but was only released under the designation MPU-104.
keywords: Routes one of 5 MIDI inputs to the output
Can also function as a MIDI splitter (one input to 5 alternative outputs)
Optional external PSA power adapter for LED indicator

name: MPU-105 MIDI Output Selector
description: The MPU-105 MIDI Output Selector is a MIDI-Thru box in a 1/2 19" housing. The signal from the MIDI IN jack can be routed to 5 MIDI THRU ports, which can be individually switched on or off. A red LED indicates power supply (via PSA-series AC adapter), and a green LED indicates incoming MIDI data. Furthermore, LEDs show which MIDI THRU jacks (1 to 5) are active. Unlike the MPU-104, the MPU-105 cannot be reversed in function or operated without a power supply. The MPU-105 was initially intended to be named MI-50 but was only released under the designation MPU-105.
keywords: Individual On/Off Switches for Each THRU Port
Green LED for MIDI Data Reception

name: MSQ-100 Digital MIDI-Keyboard Recorder
description: The MSQ-100 is a simple, single-track MIDI sequencer capable of recording data from all 16 MIDI channels. Notes can be recorded via real-time recording or step input, and overdubs are possible (e.g., to record data from other MIDI channels in subsequent passes). The MSQ-100 can operate as a master or slave (both MIDI and DIN SYNC) and data can be stored on tape/cassette recorders (using an FSK signal, which can also be recorded with an HD recorder nowadays). The MSQ-100 does not have detailed editing functions and can thus be seen as the MIDI successor to the CSQ-100 or the DCB version JSQ-60. Switches on the rear allow individual settings for whether aftertouch, pitch bend, controller data, or velocity (note-on velocity) are recorded or not. The MSQ-100 offers memory for approximately 3000 notes (velocity enabled) or 6100 notes (velocity disabled).
keywords: Records data from all 16 MIDI channels
Data storage to tape/cassette recorder via FSK signal
Rear panel switches for recording Aftertouch, Pitch Bend, Controller data, and Velocity
Memory for approx. 3000 notes (velocity ON) or 6100 notes (velocity OFF)
Includes PSA power supply and 2 MSC MIDI cables

name: PG-300 Programmer
description: The PG-300 is a programmer, a device with sliders, buttons, and switches for programming sounds for MKS-50, Alpha Juno-1, and Juno-2. Programming is done via System Exclusive (SysEx) data, which is sent over MIDI when one of the PG-300's controls is moved.
keywords: Sliders, buttons, and switches for sound programming
Compatible with Roland MKS-50, Alpha Juno-1, and Juno-2
Sends System Exclusive (SysEx) data over MIDI

name: RS-202 String Ensemble
description: The Roland Strings RS-202 is a polyphonic, analog keyboard with 61 non-velocity-sensitive keys for generating string imitations. The RS-202 is firmly built into an instrument case, from which the lid can be removed. The RS-202 has two keyboard zones for which the total of 3 sounds can be switched on and off independently. The Brass sound and the two String sounds can be separately adjusted in tone, and a fixed-frequency vibrato's intensity can be controlled for the entire keyboard. For each keyboard zone, the volume can be slightly attenuated with a rocker switch, and the attack time can be switched between Slow and Fast. A master volume control is available. Compared to its predecessor, the RS-101, the ability to delay vibrato and, primarily, the 3-position Ensemble switch (Bypass, I, and II) have been added. This is the typical Roland chorus effect. There is no headphone output, but only two line outputs that carry the same mono signal at higher and lower levels.
keywords: Built-in instrument case with removable lid
Individual tone control for Brass and String sounds
Volume attenuation and attack time (Slow/Fast) per zone
3-position Ensemble switch (Bypass, I, II) for Roland chorus effect
Internal power supply with fixed power cable

name: Roland 101 System 100
description: The foundation of the System-100 synthesizer. This basic unit is a completely self-contained, monophonic analog synthesizer equipped with a 37-key keyboard and the following synthesizer components: VCO, noise generator, audio mixer, high-pass filter, VCF, VCA, envelope generator (ADSR), LFO, and glide.

name: Roland 101 System 100, 101 Basic Unit
description: The cornerstone of the System-100 synthesizer. This basic unit is a fully standalone, monophonic analog synthesizer equipped with a 37-key keyboard and the following synthesizer modules: VCO, Noise Generator, Audio Mixer, High Pass Filter, VCF, VCA, Envelope Generator (ADSR), LFO, Glide. Pulse width is variable. CV and GATE inputs and outputs are available.

name: Roland 102
description: The 102 is a monophonic analog synthesizer expander unit for the System-100.  It's similar in design to the 101, featuring a VCO, noise generator, audio mixer, high-pass filter, VCF, VCA, ADSR envelope generator, and LFO with glide. Pulse width is variable. Unlike the 101, it lacks a keyboard but includes a ring modulator, sample and hold, and a mixing unit.  CV and gate inputs and outputs are present.

name: Roland 102 System 100, 102 Expander Unit
description: The 102 Synthesizer Expander of the System-100 is a complete, monophonic analog synthesizer and is similar in structure to the 101: VCO, Noise Generator, Audio Mixer, High Pass Filter, VCF, VCA, Envelope Generator (ADSR), LFO, Glide. The pulse width is variable. Compared to the 101, it lacks a keyboard, but additionally features a Ring Modulator, Sample & Hold, and a mixer unit. CV and GATE inputs and outputs are available.
keywords: Components: VCO, Noise Generator, Audio Mixer, High Pass Filter, VCF, VCA, Envelope Generator (ADSR), LFO, Glide
CV and GATE inputs and outputs

name: Roland 103 System 100 Audio Mixer
description: The Roland 103 is a 4-channel stereo mixer from the System-100 series. It's designed to connect four mono signal sources. Inputs can be switched between MIC, Line Hi, and Line Low levels, and distributed in the stereo panorama using the pan control.  Each channel allows adjustment of the effect level (send control), with a choice between external effects or an internal reverb spring. The 103 Mixer also has a stereo power amplifier with 2 x 2.5 watts at 8 ohms for use with matching 109 speakers.
keywords: 2 x 2.5W stereo power amp at 8 ohms

name: Roland 103 System 100, 103 Audio Mixer
description: The 4-channel stereo mixer 103 of the System-100 is designed for connecting 4 mono signal sources. The inputs can be switched from MIC to Line Hi and Line Low levels and panned within the stereo panorama. For each channel, the effect amount (Send control) can be set, and a switch allows choosing between an external effect loop or an internal spring reverb. Additionally, the 103 mixer has a stereo power amplifier with 2 x 2.5 watts into 8 ohms for the matching 109 speakers.
keywords: Switchable inputs: MIC, Line Hi, Line Low
Switchable between external effect loop or internal spring reverb
Integrated stereo power amplifier (2 x 2.5 watts at 8 ohms)

name: Roland 104 System 100, 104 Sequencer
description: The Roland 104 is an analog step sequencer for the System-100.  It features two channels with up to 12 steps each, adjustable step count, and selectable voltage ranges (2.5V, 5V, 10V).  Gate time and clock rate are globally adjustable.  This sequencer is notable for its directly adjustable control voltages for each step.
keywords: Two channels with up to 12 steps each
Adjustable gate time and clock rate

name: Roland 109 System 100 Monitor Speaker Set
description: The Roland 109 is a pair of monitor speakers designed for the System-100. Each speaker has two 16cm full-range speakers with 8 ohms impedance and a maximum power handling of 3.5W.

name: Roland 109 System 100, 109 Monitor Speaker Set (2 Stück)
description: The 109 speaker module for the System-100 consists of a pair of speaker cabinets with two 16cm full-range speakers, each at 8 Ohm and a maximum power handling of 3.5W. The dimensions refer to a single speaker cabinet.
keywords: Roland 109 System 100, 109 Monitor Speaker Set (2 Stück)
Passive speakers (no internal power supply needed)

name: Roland 110 System 100M VCO/VCF/VCA Module
description: A combined VCO, VCF, and VCA module for the System-100M synthesizer. It contains three core synthesizer elements: VCO, VCF, and VCA.  When paired with the 140 module (ENV 1/2, LFO), it provides all the necessary components for sound generation. The combination of modules 110 and 140 enables control of each individual function unit. The VCO, VCF, and VCA units are internally connected within the 110 module. These internal connections significantly reduce the number of external cable connections.  When using external connections, internal connections are automatically interrupted. An internal connection, when using the 140 module, allows simultaneous control of VCF and VCA in the 110 module via the 140's envelope generator.

name: Roland 112
description: The Roland 112 module offers two VCOs for the System-100M. This module houses two independent VCOs with numerous switching options. Each VCO has three separate, adjustable control inputs, a switch for strong and weak signals, and both manual and external control of pulse width.
keywords: Manual and external pulse width control

name: Roland 121
description: The Roland 121 is a dual voltage-controlled low-pass filter (VCF) module for the System-100M synthesizer.  It houses two independent VCFs, each with a fixed high-pass filter offering three selectable cutoff frequencies.  Each VCF also has three audio inputs and three control inputs.  Green LEDs indicate signal output, and red LEDs show clipping.
keywords: LED indicators for output and clipping

name: Roland 121 System 100M, 2 VCF Modul
description: The 121 module provides two Voltage Controlled Filters (VCFs) for the System-100M. This module houses two voltage-controlled and independent LOW-PASS filters. Each VCF is additionally equipped with a fixed High-Pass Filter, featuring a switch for three possible cutoff frequencies. Furthermore, each VCF has three audio inputs and three control inputs. Green LED indicators illuminate when a signal reaches the output, while red LEDs indicate clipping.
keywords: Two independent Voltage Controlled Low-Pass Filters (VCFs)
Fixed High-Pass Filter per VCF with 3 selectable cutoff frequencies
Green LED indicator for output signal presence
Designed for the Roland System-100M modular synthesizer system

name: Roland 130 System 100M, 2 VCA Modul
description: Dual VCA module 130 for the System-100M. Each VCA has a switch for linear or exponential control and three audio and three control inputs.

name: Roland 131
description: The Roland 131 is an output mixer module for the System-100M synthesizer.  It features four inputs with individual level and pan controls, separate master volume and headphone controls, and a tuning oscillator with selectable frequencies (220, 440, 880 Hz).  Outputs include stereo mini and standard jacks, and each output features an overload LED.
keywords: 4 inputs with level and pan controls

name: Roland 131 System 100M, Output Mixer
description: The 131 Output Mixer Module for the System-100M features four inputs, each with a slider for level control and a rotary knob for pan-pot. It has separate volume controls for Master Volume and Headphone Jack, and a tuning oscillator (for tuning other oscillators) with a frequency switch (220, 440, 880 Hz) and a rotary knob for its volume. The outputs (Stereo out Left/Right and Mono out) are equipped for both mini-jack and standard jack. Additionally, each output is fitted with an LED overload indicator (from 110 dB).
keywords: Output mixer module for Roland System-100M
Four inputs with level sliders and pan-pots
Separate Master Volume and Headphone Jack controls
Integrated tuning oscillator with frequency switch (220, 440, 880 Hz) and volume control
Stereo Left/Right and Mono outputs (mini-jack and standard jack)
LED overload indicator on each output (from 110 dB)

name: Roland 131 System 100M, Output Mixer
description: The Output Mixer Module 131 for the System-100M features four inputs, each with a slider for level control and a rotary knob for pan-pot. It has separate volume controls for master volume and headphone jack, and a tuning oscillator (for tuning other oscillators) with a frequency switch (220, 440, 880 Hz) and a rotary knob for its volume. The outputs (Stereo out Left/Right and Mono out) are equipped for mini-jack and standard jack. Additionally, each output is fitted with an LED indicator for overload (from 110 dB).
keywords: Output mixer module for Roland System-100M
Four inputs with individual level control and pan-pot
Separate master volume and headphone jack volume controls
Tuning oscillator with frequency switch (220, 440, 880 Hz)

name: Roland 132
description: The Roland 132 is a dual CV/Audio mixer and processor module for the System-100M. It features two 4-channel mixers with direct and inverted outputs, usable for mixing audio signals or control voltages.  It includes voltage processors for positive and negative variable voltages. High studio quality with a noise level above 90dB
keywords: Positive and negative variable voltage processors

name: Roland 132 System 100M, Dual C/V Audio Mixer and Voltage Processor
description: The Roland 132 is a Dual CV/Audio Mixer and Processor Module for the System-100M. It features two 4-channel mixers with direct and inverted outputs, capable of mixing both audio signals and control voltages. Two channels are equipped with positive and negative fixed voltages, which can also be used as normal mixer channels via patch jacks. A red LED indicates output overload (distortion). The Voltage Processor consists of two sections, one for positive and one for negative variable voltage. The mixer's frequency range extends from DC to 40 kHz AC, and with a signal-to-noise ratio of more than 90 dB, this module offers highest studio quality.
keywords: Roland 132 System 100M, Dual C/V Audio Mixer and Voltage Processor
Dual CV/Audio Mixer and Processor module
Part of the Roland System-100M modular synthesizer series
Direct and inverted outputs for each mixer
Suitable for mixing both audio signals and control voltages (CV)
Two channels with positive and negative fixed voltages (patchable as regular mixer channels)
Red LED indicator for output overload/distortion
Voltage Processor section with positive and negative variable voltage outputs
Mixer frequency range: DC (direct current) to 40 kHz AC (alternating current)
Power supplied via Roland 190, 191, or 191J module cases

name: Roland 140 System 100M, 2 Env/LFO Modul
description: The Module 140 offers 2 envelope generators and LFOs for the System-100M. Together with Module 110, this component provides the necessary elements to produce synthesizer sounds. When used with Modules 112, 121, and 130, enough elements are available to achieve two voices simultaneously. The LFO (Voltage Controlled Low Frequency Oscillator) with built-in delay allows for delay vibrato effects. The Keyboard/Trigger switch enables phase-locking of the LFO output with the keyboard trigger impulse. The envelopes (ADSR) can be triggered either manually via a rotary knob, via trigger gate, or via an internal/external gate.
keywords: LFOs with built-in delay for delay vibrato effects
Multiple triggering options for envelopes (manual, trigger gate, internal/external gate)
Enables two-voice operation when combined with other modules (112, 121, 130)

name: Roland 140 System 100M, 2 Env/LFO Module
description: The 140 module provides two envelope generators and LFOs for the System-100M.  Combined with the 110 module, it provides the essential elements for producing synthesizer sounds. When used with modules 112, 121, and 130, enough elements are available to create two voices simultaneously. The LFO (voltage-controlled low-frequency oscillator) with built-in delay allows for delay/vibrato effects. The keyboard/trigger switch allows phase locking of the LFO output with the keyboard trigger pulse. The envelopes (ADSR) can be triggered manually via a rotary knob, via trigger gate, or via an internal/external gate.

name: Roland 150
description: The Roland 150 module for the System-100M includes a ring modulator, a sample and hold unit, and an LFO.  The ring modulator combines two VCO outputs to create metallic-sounding tones. The sample and hold function is a random generator that automatically creates sound patterns based on the input waveform.

name: Roland 150 System 100M Ring, Noise, S&H, LFO Module
description: The Module 150 for the System-100M is a versatile module incorporating a ring modulator, a Sample & Hold (S&H) circuit, and a Low Frequency Oscillator (LFO). The ring modulator's primary function is to combine two VCO outputs to create distinctive metallic-sounding tones. The Sample & Hold unit acts as a random generator, automatically producing tone patterns based on the input waveform.
keywords: Roland 150 System 100M Ring, Noise, S&H, LFO Module
Ring Modulator for combining VCO outputs
Sample & Hold (S&H) circuit for random tone pattern generation
Designed as a module for the Roland System-100M modular synthesizer
Requires power supply from 190, 191, or 191J module cases

name: Roland 150 System 100M, Ring, Noise, S&H, LFO Modul
description: The Module 150 for the System-100M includes a Ring Modulator, Sample & Hold unit, and an LFO. The main function of the Ring Modulator is to combine two VCO outputs to create metallic-sounding tones. Sample & Hold: This random generator automatically produces tonal patterns according to the input waveform.
keywords: Roland 150 System 100M, Ring, Noise, S&H, LFO Modul
Ring Modulator combines two VCO outputs for metallic tones
Sample & Hold generates random tonal patterns

name: Roland 165
description: The Roland 165 is a double portamento module for the System-100M. It features two independent portamento units that transform glissando signals into genuine portamentos, controllable via control voltages.

name: Roland 165 System 100M Module, PORTAMENTO CONTROLLER
description: The double Portamento Module 165 for the System-100M contains two separate, equivalent portamento units. These units convert glissando signals into true portamento effects. These portamentos can in turn be activated by targeted control voltages, for example, by the MC-4: Portamento CV, MPX = Multiplex.
keywords: Double portamento module for Roland System-100M
Portamento activatable via control voltages (e.g., MC-4)
Power supplied via 190, 191, or 191J module housings
Recommended accessories: 190, 191, 191J module housings, 180, 181, 184 CV/Gate keyboards, other System-100M modules (110 to 182)

name: Roland 172
description: The Roland 172 module is a Phase Shifter, Audio Delay, and Gate Delay unit for the System-100M.  It offers spatial effects, a flanger effect (when combining Phase Shifter and Audio Delay), and voltage control.  A built-in LFO provides normal and inverted outputs. The Gate Delay allows delayed gate signals, shortening of gate impulses, and amplification of recorded gate impulses for triggering synthesizer functions.

name: Roland 173
description: The SIGNAL GATE / MULTIPLE JACK Module 173 for the System-100M consists of 4 signal gates with an additional patchbay. name: Roland 717 A System-700, Sequencer
description: The Roland 717A is a module of the System-700 and contains an analog step sequencer. It is the largest module of the System-700, occupying an entire block (BLOCK 3). Unlike competing modular sequencers, the 717A can be used immediately and does not require internal patching with cables. The 717A is designed as a three-channel, 12-step sequencer and thus has 36 rotary controls whose CV voltage must be set. These 36 controls can be switched in series, providing a total of 36 steps, or in parallel mode, providing three independent rows for controlling, for example, pitch (row 1), timbre (row 2), and volume (row 3). The set sequence cannot be stored, but – as with all analog step sequencers – individual values can be quickly changed with their own knob while the sequence is running. Each row of controls, called a channel, has a three-position switch for setting the control voltage (2 Volt, 4 Volt, and 10 Volt). The duration of each step can be set jointly for all three channels via a multi-stage rotary switch that offers divisions of 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, and 1/32. For each step, common to all channels, there is also a control for fine-tuning the time values, allowing dotted notes, accelerandi, and rubati. With the help of the step selector, one can choose how many of the maximum 16 steps per channel should actually be used, allowing unwanted pauses to be skipped. One can also limit the use to various channels, i.e., only Channel A, Channel A and B in series, or all three channels in series for the maximum possible 36 steps. The internal clock oscillator is used for sequence speed control. Alternatively, an external clock signal can be used. The pulse-width rotary control in the clock oscillator section sets the gate time per note.

name: Roland AF-100 'Bee Baa' Treble Booster
description: The Roland AF-100 'Bee Baa' is a floor effect pedal for guitar housed in a sturdy metal casing. It is a combined treble booster and fuzz effect. A switch on the top allows switching between both effects. The 'FUZZ TONE SELECT' switch to its left changes the timbre of the fuzz effect. The switch on the right toggles between the effect and normal signal. Unusually, the jacks and controls are located on the narrow rear side. On the far right is the mono jack input labeled 'TO GUITAR', three controls for the fuzz: SUSTAIN, TONE, and VOLUME, the 'ADJ.' control for the booster, and on the left, the jack output labeled 'TO AMP'. Turning the Fuzz SUSTAIN control all the way to the left (OFF position) audibly deactivates the fuzz. To change the battery, loosen the two rear-side screws and lift the top of the housing. The silver casing was also used for the AG-5 'Funny Cat'. According to company founder Ikutaro Kakehashi, the name 'Bee Baa' is understood by listening to the sound. The AF-100 was manufactured by the Roland Music Engineering Group, or Roland MEG, which was later renamed 'Boss'.

TONE adjusts the sound character of the fuzz distortion, OUT LEVEL adjusts the output level. The input jack labeled INSTRUMENT (6.3mm mono jack) is on the right side, while the mono output jack 'OUTPUT' is on the left. To change the battery, the casing must be unscrewed from the bottom; mains operation is not provided. The housing shape is the same as that used for (Roland) AS-1, AP-2, and (Boss) BF-1. The AF-60 was manufactured by the Roland Music Engineering Group, or Roland MEG, which was later renamed 'Boss'.

name: Roland AP-2 'Phase II' Phaser-Pedal
description: The Roland AP-2 'Phase II' is a floor effect pedal for guitar in a sturdy, medium-brown die-cast casing. It is a phaser with two controls, RATE and RESONANCE, and an effect/bypass switch on the top. RATE controls the modulation speed, RESONANCE controls the tonal character of the phaser. The 'INSTRUMENT' jack input is on the left side, unlike most other Roland effects, and the output (jack, mono) is on the right. This complicates cabling multiple effects. To change the two (!!) 9V block batteries, the casing must be unscrewed from the bottom; power supply operation is not provided. The casing shape is the same as used for (Roland) AS-1, AF-60, and (Boss) BF-1. The AP-2 'Phase II' was manufactured by the Roland Music Engineering Group (Roland MEG), which was later renamed 'Boss'.

name: Roland AP-2 ´Phase II´
description: The Roland AP-2 ´Phase II´ is a guitar pedal housed in a durable, medium-brown diecast case.  It's a phaser with two controls: RATE and RESONANCE, and an effect/bypass switch on top. RATE adjusts the modulation speed, RESONANCE adjusts the phaser's tone.  The ´INSTRUMENT´ jack input is on the left, unlike most other Roland effects, and the output (mono jack) is on the right. This makes connecting multiple effects more difficult. To change the two 9V block batteries, the bottom of the case must be unscrewed; it does not have a power supply.

name: Roland AP-5 ´Phase Five´
description: The Roland AP-5 ´Phase Five´ is a guitar pedal housed in a sturdy, black die-cast case.  It features three switches: one for selecting between effect and normal signal, one for switching between continuous control (LFO) and touch control (input signal level), and one for adjusting speed in continuous control mode.  Four knobs control sensitivity, intensity, and modulation speed.  It has a built-in power supply with a fixed power cord.

name: Roland AP-5 ´Phase Five´ Phaser-Pedal
description: The Roland AP-5 'Phase Five' Phaser is a guitar floor effects pedal housed in a sturdy, black die-cast enclosure. This phaser features three switches on the front top: on the left, a toggle between EFFECT and NORMAL signal; in the middle, a toggle from C.C. (Continuous Control, controlled by the built-in LFO) to T.C. (Touch Control, controlled by the input signal level); and on the right, a toggle from SLOW to FAST in C.C. mode. On the rear top right, there's the power toggle switch, next to which are four controls for adjusting the phaser: SENSITIVITY determines how responsively the phaser reacts to the input signal in T.C. mode; INTENSITY controls the modulation depth; the two REPEAT RATE controls adjust the modulation speed for Slow and Fast in C.C. operation. Both connection jacks (6.3mm mono jack) are located on the left edge of the rear: furthest left is the 'INSTRUMENT' input, next to it 'OUTPUT'. The enclosure shape is the same as later used for the Roland AP-7 and slightly modified for (Boss) CE-1, DB-5, and DM-1. The AP-5 has a built-in power supply with a permanently attached power cable on the right rear. Battery operation is not supported. The AP-5 is Roland's first phaser and was manufactured by the Roland Music Engineering Group (Roland MEG), which was later renamed 'Boss'.

name: Roland CR-1000
description: The Roland CR-1000 Digital Drummer is a flat, digital rhythm machine with 24 fixed rhythms and MIDI.  Rhythm patterns are grouped into 3 selectable groups of 8 patterns each. Each rhythm offers a variation, 4 fills, an intro, and an ending, all selectable via illuminated buttons. An additional button adds handclaps.  Larger buttons start/stop and trigger fill-ins. Eight mini-sliders and a 3-digit LED display (showing tempo) are on the front panel.  Sliders control accent strength, groove (straight to heavily shuffled), and individual volume for bass drum, snare/rim/clap, timbale/toms, cymbals/hi-hat, conga, and claves/cowbell. Tempo is set via a large knob (28-249 BPM) or external MIDI clock sync. A smaller volume knob is also present. The rear panel has three footswitch jacks (Start/Stop, Fill-In, Restart), mono output, MIDI In and Thru, power jack and on/off switch. It can run on AC adapter or 6 AA batteries.

name: Roland CR-5000
description: The Roland 'CompuRhythm CR-5000 Micro Computer Controlled Rhythm Machine' is an analog rhythm machine with fixed pre-programmed rhythms in a console-style housing. The front part of the housing is slanted and contains the controls for rhythm selection: with three group and 8 selection buttons, one of 24 basic rhythm patterns can be selected; a rotary switch allows setting one of eight fill-patterns and another determines whether the fill-pattern is played at all, or every 2, 4, 8, 12, or 16 bars. Another button is used to manually trigger the fill-pattern. With 6 additional buttons, you can add a cymbal (quarter notes or 8th), a hi-hat (eighth or 16th), open hi-hat (16th) and/or conga. A CRASH button adds an analog crash cymbal sound after a fill or intro. START/STOP buttons, a tempo control (40 to 320 BPM), a tempo-synced 'pilot lamp' (LED), and a SHUFFLE button are also located on the slanted main control panel. Behind the slanted main control panel are the power switch and 7 volume controls: five small knobs adjust the mix ratio of 1. Bass, 2. Tom, Rim, Snare, 3. Conga, 4. Claves and Cowbell, 5. Cymbal and HiHat. Two larger knobs are for adjusting ACCENT (strength of emphasis) and overall volume. On the rear, there is an audio output (mono OUTPUT!), 4 footswitch connections (REGISTER, INTRO/FILL, RESTART, START/STOP), and a trigger output whose impulses can be selected via a slide switch between ACCent, 8th, or 16th note. The CR-5000 can only be used as a master. The CR-5000 does not allow programming custom rhythm patterns; for that, the CR-8000 was available concurrently, which is almost identical except for the USER rhythms and programming functions. The 8 fixed rhythms per group are: Waltz, Swing1, Swing2, S.Rock, Tango, Habanera, Enka, BD-4 Rock1, Rock2, Rock3, Rock4, Rock5, Rock6, Disco, FoxTrott Samba1, Samba2, Melengue, Mambo, ChaCha, Rhumba, Beguine, Bossanova.
keywords: Fixed pre-programmed rhythms (24 basic patterns, 8 fill-patterns)

name: Roland CR-5000
description: The Roland CR-5000 CompuRhythm is an analog rhythm machine with pre-programmed rhythms.  It features a slanted control panel with buttons for rhythm selection, fill patterns, and additional percussion elements.  The user can adjust the mix of various drum sounds, accent levels, and tempo.  It offers a limited level of customization but excels in its straightforward operation and preset rhythms.

name: Roland CR-68
description: The Roland CR-68 CompuRhythm is an analog rhythm machine featuring 19 built-in rhythms selectable via push buttons.  Seven additional fill-in rhythms or a pause can be triggered manually or automatically every 2, 4, 8, 12, or 16 bars. Controls include accent and balance for adjusting emphasis and high-frequency instrument levels, respectively.  Tempo and volume are adjustable, and it includes start/stop buttons.  The unit has a mono output (high and low impedance jacks), connections for start/stop and variation buttons, and a trigger output switchable between eighth and sixteenth notes.

name: Roland CR-68 CompuRhythm
description: The Roland CR-68 rhythm machine, externally named "CompuRhythm CR-68", is an analog rhythm machine with 19 fixed rhythms that can be selected via push buttons. Seven additional fill-in rhythms or a pause can be triggered manually via a button, or automatically every 2, 4, 8, 12, or 16 bars via a rotary switch. An ACCENT knob allows adjusting the intensity of accents, and a BALANCE knob controls the volume proportion of high-frequency instruments in the overall sound. TEMPO and VOLUME knobs, START/STOP button, and power switch are also on the front of the CR-68, which is housed in a rectangular wooden casing. On the rear, there is a mono output (2 jacks for high and low levels), two connections for buttons (Start/Stop and Variation), and a trigger impulse output, switchable between 8th and 16th notes. The tempo can only be adjusted via the rotary knob and is indicated by an LED on the front. External synchronization is not possible. The CR-68 and CR-78 represent the third generation of Roland rhythm machines. The rhythms, each with a variation, include: Rock 1, Rock 2, Rock 3, Rock 4, Disco 1, Disco 2, Waltz, Shuffle, Slow Rock, Swing, Fox Trot (Variation: Tango), Boogie, Enka, Bossa Nova, Samba, Mambo (Variation: Cha Cha), Beguine (Variation: Rhumba).
keywords: Connections for external Start/Stop and Variation buttons
Rhythms include: Rock 1-4, Disco 1-2, Waltz, Shuffle, Slow Rock, Swing, Fox Trot (Tango), Boogie, Enka, Bossa Nova, Samba, Mambo (Cha Cha), Beguine (Rhumba)

name: Roland CR-78
description: The Roland CR-78 rhythm machine, externally named 'CompuRhythm CR-78', features analog sound generation with 34 fixed rhythms selectable via push buttons. 11 additional variations can be pre-selected as fill-ins and triggered manually or automatically every 2, 4, 8, 12, or 16 measures via a rotary switch. The CompuRhythm CR-78 offers 4 additional, freely programmable (1-bar) rhythms and is notable as the first programmable rhythm machine. Users can select 4 out of 10 instruments for programming custom rhythms using a rotary switch. Step programming requires the separately sold 'Program Switch' WS-1, a small box with 2 buttons and a 3-pin jack cable. An ACCENT knob adjusts the intensity of accents, and TEMPO controls the speed, indicated by a measure-by-measure blinking LED. Slider controls include BALANCE for adjusting the volume ratio of high-frequency instruments, VOLUME for overall loudness, and CY-HH-METALIC BEAT, TAMBOURIN, GUIRO for fading these instruments in and out. Push buttons allow muting BASS DRUM, SNARE, COWBELL/CLAVES, and CYMBAL/HIGH HAT within a rhythm. There are also two 3-stage toggle switches for controlling the length (LONG, SHORT, OFF) of a fade-in and a fade-out. START/STOP buttons and the power switch are on the front. The rear panel features a mono output (2 jacks for high and low level), three inputs for footswitches (Start/Stop, Memory, and Variation), and a trigger impulse input/output switchable between 8th and 16th notes. The CR-78 rhythm machine is housed in a rectangular wooden cabinet, available in both wood finish and black. The CR-78 and CR-68 represent the third generation of Roland rhythm devices, with the CR-78 being the more interesting due to its versatile combination possibilities, synchronizability, and especially its programmable patterns. In addition to the four programmable rhythm patterns, the following fixed rhythms (each with one variation) are available: Rock 1, Rock 2, Rock 3, Rock 4, Disco 1, Disco 2, Waltz, Shuffle, Slow Rock, Swing, Fox Trot (Variation: Tango), Boogie, Enka, Bossa Nova, Samba, Mambo (Variation: Cha Cha), Beguine (Variation: Rhumba).
keywords: Individual instrument level faders (e.g., Metallic Beat, Tambourine, Guiro)
Mute switches for Bass Drum, Snare, Cowbell/Claves, Cymbal/High Hat

name: Roland CR-78
description: The Roland CR-78 CompuRhythm is an analog rhythm machine with 34 built-in rhythms selectable via push buttons.  It features 11 additional variations as fill-ins, manually or automatically triggered every 2, 4, 8, 12, or 16 beats.  The CR-78 also offers 4 programmable one-beat rhythms, making it one of the first programmable rhythm machines.  Users can select 4 out of 10 instruments for programming their own rhythms. Step programming requires the optional WS-1 programming switch.  Accent and tempo controls are provided, with a blinking LED indicating the beat.  Sliders control balance, volume, and the presence of cymbal/high hat, tambourine, and guiro. Push buttons mute bass drum, snare, cowbell/claves, and cymbal/high hat.  Fade-in and fade-out lengths are adjustable.  It features mono output (high and low impedance), trigger input/output, and connections for external switches. The CR-78 was available in both wood and black finishes.

name: Roland CSQ-100
description: The CSQ-100 is a digitally controlled sequencer for analog CV/Gate signals. It stores two 84-step sequences that can be played independently or together, once or repeatedly. It includes a CV input for transposition, as well as START and STEP output jacks. Step duration and CV voltages are programmed in two separate passes.  Sequences are briefly stored in memory by a battery after switching off; there is no additional save function.

name: Roland CSQ-100 Computer Sequencer
description: The CSQ-100 is a digitally controlled sequencer for analog CV/Gate signals. It offers memory for 2 sequences of 84 steps (notes) each, which can be played independently or chained, once or repeatedly. A CV input for transposition is available, as are START and STEP output jacks. Step duration and CV voltages can be programmed separately in two passes. Recorded sequences are temporarily backed up by a battery even after power-off; there is no option to permanently save sequences. The CSQ-100 is Roland's first sequencer whose steps could only be entered or played via a CV/Gate keyboard. At the time, the MC-8 (later replaced by the MC-4) existed for programming, and module 182 for adjusting individual steps. The CSQ-100 was directly followed by the larger CSQ-600, after which the concept was consistently implemented for new control technologies, first DCB, then MIDI, leading to the JSQ-60 and MSQ-100 models.

name: Roland CSQ-600
description: The CSQ-600 is a digitally controlled sequencer for analog CV/Gate signals. It features four sequences, each with a maximum of 150 steps (notes).  Sequences are retained in memory even after power off thanks to a built-in battery.  The four sequences can be combined in any order. CV and step time can be recorded separately in two passes, and external (slave) synchronization is possible.  Note that while the internal battery retains sequences temporarily after power down, there's no provision for permanent saving.

name: Roland D-10 LA
description: The D-10 is a 9-part multitimbral, 32-voice digital synthesizer with 61 velocity-sensitive keys and MIDI.  It uses LA synthesis, combining PCM samples without a filter and simpler synthesis with a filter.  A "Timbre" consists of two "Tones", each made of one or two "Partials". A partial can be a PCM oscillator or a simple pulse-width-modulated oscillator. The filter is warm-sounding and offers resonance.  It includes a drum computer for creating songs from 1- to 2-bar patterns.  It features two modes: Performance (layering or splitting two sounds) and Multitimbral (controlling 8 parts simultaneously via MIDI).

name: Roland D-10 LA-Synthesizer
description: The D-10 is a 9-part multi-timbral, 32-voice digital synthesizer with 61 velocity-sensitive synthesizer keys and MIDI. 8 tonally playable parts (sub-synthesizers) and one rhythm part utilize LA synthesis, a combination of PCM samples without filters and simpler synthesis with filters. A sound program is called 'Timbre' and consists of 2 'Tones', which in turn are formed from one or two 'Partials'. A Partial is either a PCM oscillator (ROM samples) with a subsequent amplifier or it consists of a simple, pulse-width modifiable oscillator (triangle/square wave) with a dynamic filter and amplifier. 13 structures are selectable for connecting the two Partials to a Tone, so a sound program (Timbre) can consist of up to 4 oscillators. The filter offers resonance without self-oscillation and sounds exceptionally 'warm'. The 256 internally available PCM samples are slightly shorter than those of the first LA synthesizer D-50. The sound generation is the same as in the D-5, D-20, and D-110, concluding with a digital reverb offering 8 algorithms. For easier programming, a PG-10 programmer can be connected. The D-10 and other models in the D-series were the first synthesizers to have demo songs in ROM. The D-10 has a built-in drum computer with which one can compose a song from 1- to 2-bar patterns or play sounds manually in Manual mode. There are 32 preset and 32 freely programmable patterns. The D-10 has two operating modes, Performance and Multitimbral. For live performance, two sounds (parts) can be layered or split in Performance mode. In Multitimbral mode, 8 parts can be controlled simultaneously via MIDI. 128 Performances, 64 Tones, and 64 Timbres can be stored internally; an inserted M-128 or M-256 memory card doubles the memory.

name: Roland D-5 LA
description: The D-5 is a 9-part multitimbral, 32-voice digital synthesizer with 61 velocity-sensitive keys, arpeggiator, and MIDI.  It uses LA synthesis, combining two tones via 13 structures. A tone consists of a PCM oscillator or a simple oscillator.  Sound generation is similar to the D-10, D-20, and D-110. It has an external power supply and a lower-quality keyboard compared to the D-10.

name: Roland D-50
description: The Roland D-50 is a 16-voice digital synthesizer known for its Linear Arithmetic (LA) synthesis.  This innovative method combines PCM samples with analog synthesis for unique sounds.  It features 61 keys, aftertouch, and a built-in arpeggiator.  The D-50 was one of the first synthesizers to incorporate onboard digital effects.

name: Roland D-50 LA Synthesizer, MIDI
description: The D-50 is a 16-voice digital synthesizer with 61 velocity-sensitive synthesizer keys, channel aftertouch, a pitch bend/modulation lever, and a freely adjustable MIDI channel. The D-50 is not multitimbral. It was the first synthesizer to use ROM samples as waveforms for its oscillators, a sound generation method called LA Synthesis. A sound program, called a patch, consists of two Tones, which in turn are composed of 2 Partials linked via one of 7 structures. A Partial can be an analog synthesizer (oscillator, filter, amp) or a PCM sample. The D-50 was also the first synthesizer with built-in audio effects. A special programmer (PG-1000) can be connected for programming sounds.

LA synthesis creates sounds using two tones, each composed of two partials linked by one of seven structures.  A partial can be an analog synthesizer (oscillator, filter, amp) or a PCM sample.  The D-50 was the first synth with built-in effects; this feature is also present in the D-550.  It can be edited with the PG-1000 programmer.

The keyboard supports four zones with layering and splitting, each with individual channel settings.

name: Roland D-70 Super LA Synthesizer
description: The D-70 is a 6-part multi-timbral, digital MIDI synthesizer with 76 velocity-sensitive synthesizer keys and Channel Aftertouch. The so-called Advanced LA synthesis sound engine of the D-70 is a maximum 30-voice evolution of the U- and D-series, combining up to 4 Tones with PCM oscillators and dynamic filters. Originally, the D-70 was intended to be called U-50, as its sound engine builds upon the U-series and can utilize ROM samples from SN-U110 cards for the U-series. However, the dynamic filters were adopted from the D-series. The keyboard can supply 4 zones with layer and split sounds, with the send channel for each zone being separately enabled and configured.

name: Roland DJ-70
description: The DJ-70 is a stereo sampler with a 3-octave velocity-sensitive keyboard.  It's 24-voice, 31-part multitimbral, and features an 8-track sequencer with RPS (real-time playback). It uses the same data format as the S-700 series, layering up to 4 samples into partials, with up to 88 forming a patch. Each partial has dynamic amps and filters with resonance.  The DJ-70 can load samples while playing and also processes sound disks from the S-330 and S-550. It has 2MB of sample memory, expandable to 4MB, using only floppy disk drives (DD and HD). A unique feature is the scratch dial for sampling sounds like vinyl scratching.

name: Roland DJ-70MKII
description: The Roland DJ-70MKII is a DJ sampling workstation with a 3-octave velocity-sensitive keyboard, 24-voice polyphony, 31-part multitimbrality, and an 8-track sequencer with RPS. It uses the same data format as the S-700 series, layering up to 4 samples into partials, with up to 88 partials forming a patch. Each partial has dynamic amps and filters with resonance. The DJ-70MKII can load samples while playing and process sound disks from the S-330 and S-550. It has 4MB of sample memory, expandable to 32MB, and uses floppy disks (DD and HD) and SCSI hard drives for storage. A unique feature is the Scratch Dial, which allows for scratching samples like vinyl records. Data written by the DJ-70MKII cannot be read by other S-700 series devices.

name: Roland DJ-70MKII
description: The Roland DJ-70MKII is a stereo sampler featuring a 3-octave velocity-sensitive keyboard. It's 24-voice, 31-part multitimbral, and includes an 8-track sequencer with RPS (real-time playback).  It uses the same data format as the S-700 series, layering up to 4 samples in partials to form patches of up to 88 samples. Each partial offers dynamic amps and filters with resonance.  The DJ-70MKII can load samples while playing and process sound disks from the S-330 and S-550. It has 4MB of sample memory, expandable to 32MB. Storage is via floppy disk drive (DD and HD) and SCSI-connected hard drives.  A unique feature is the scratch dial, allowing for turntable-style scratching of samples. Data written by the DJ-70MKII is not readable by other devices in the S-700 series.

description: The EG-101 is a Groove Arranger keyboard equipped with 49 velocity-sensitive keys, a D-Beam Controller, and an arpeggiator. name: Roland G-202
description: The Roland G-202 is a controller guitar designed for use with Roland guitar synthesizers equipped with a 24-pin connector. It features a Stratocaster-style body shape with a unique pickguard and two humbucker pickups. In addition to the 24-pin connector, which transmits individual string signals from a specialized "hexaphonic" pickup to control GR synthesizers, the G-202 also has a standard guitar output for the humbucker pickups, allowing it to be used as a regular guitar. The maple neck is bolted to an ash body, which was available in four colors: white with a black pickguard, dark blue, red, or clear-coated with a white pickguard. These variations were manufactured by Ibanez/Greco (specifically by Fuji Gen Gakki) according to Roland's specifications.  Onboard controls include four gold-colored knobs for master volume, guitar tone, cutoff frequency, and balance between guitar and synthesizer levels. Two black knobs adjust resonance (VCF) and vibrato intensity, complemented by a three-position mode switch and a three-position selector for switching between guitar, synthesizer, or a mix of both signals.

name: Roland GI-10
description: The Roland GI-10 is a Guitar-To-MIDI Interface for guitars with a 13-pin connector and GK-Pickup (GK-2, GK-3, etc.) in a 9.5-inch enclosure (1U 19-inch, half-width). It converts signals from the hexaphonic GK-Pickup into MIDI notes and other associated MIDI performance data. In addition to the GK IN jack (13-pin) on the front, there is a jack input for connecting a (normal) guitar or a microphone. If a plug is inserted here, the GI-10 no longer converts the GK-Pickup signal, but monophonically sung or played signals into MIDI data, requiring precise level control and clear separation of notes. For its primary purpose, converting a GK signal, the sensitivity for individual strings can be set in 8 steps, and it can be determined whether MIDI data should be transmitted polyphonically on an adjustable channel or in mono mode on 6 consecutive MIDI channels. The bend range can be set to 0, 2, 12, or 24 semitones, note output can be shifted up or down by 1 octave, and output for fingerpicking can be optimized in four stages, including a setting without dynamics. A tuner is built-in, with its concert pitch adjustable to either 440 Hz or 442 Hz. On the rear, an expression pedal (CC#01 or CC#11) and two footswitches can be connected via an insert cable. Footswitch 1 holds the information of the last played string and blocks new performance data, while footswitch 2 sends CC#64 (hold function/sustain/hold-1) to the connected MIDI sound generator. MIDI IN can loop through program changes, and MIDI OUT outputs the GI-10's MIDI data. The GI-10 converts guitar signals similarly to the GR-09 or GR-1, meaning one must play quite firmly and precisely. The conversion is fast, but with noticeable latency, especially for low notes. The GI-10 only converts tones with pitches within the range of a guitar. It cannot be used for converting bass signals with GK-2B or GK-3B pickups.

name: Roland GM-70 Guitar-to-MIDI-Converter
description: The Roland GM-70 is a Guitar-to-MIDI converter for G-Guitars with a 24-pin connector (G-202, G-303, G-505, G-707, G-808, or guitar with GK-1) in a 19" rack-mount chassis (1U). It converts signals from the hexaphonic pickup into MIDI notes and other associated MIDI performance data and has no internal sound generation. The GM-70 has 128 program memories where various settings can be stored as a 'patch'. A patch includes settings for up to four 'branches', which are intended for controlling four different MIDI sound generators. For each branch, you can set the MIDI base channel, pitch bending intensity, a dynamic curve, level, a program number, and the MIDI mode (monophonic, where each string sends on its own MIDI channel, or polyphonic). The assignments of various controllers to MIDI control commands are also stored in a patch. In addition to the pickup's controls, the GM-70 has rear-panel connections for two buttons and an expression pedal, as well as an RRC jack for the FC-100 pedalboard, which can each be assigned a function. GM-70 patch settings can be output via Bulk Dump over MIDI as SysEx data, saved on an external sequencer, and reloaded via MIDI IN if needed. The GM-70 has a built-in tuner, whose concert pitch can be set in 0.1 Hz steps from 430 Hz to 450 Hz. Otherwise, MIDI IN only responds to program change data. If connected MIDI sound generators cannot respond to CC#7 data (volume), their audio outputs can be connected to the STEREO IN jacks on the rear and then picked up again from the STEREO OUT jacks, where the GM-70 controls the output volume. The normal guitar signal is also mixed into STEREO OUT, unless the GUITAR OUT jack is used, where the original signal from the normal guitar pickups can be accessed. The GM-70 converts guitar signals very reliably, albeit quite slowly.

name: Roland GR-50
description: The Roland GR-50 guitar synthesizer is a compact rack-mountable guitar synthesizer system that combines a LA synthesis sound source and a MIDI converter in one powerful device. name: Roland GR-500
description: The Roland GR-500 is a polyphonic, analog guitar synthesizer with a 24-pin connection. It could only be controlled with the special GS-500 guitar.  It features five sections: Guitar input, Polyensemble, Bass, Solo synthesizer, and a control section for external synths. The GR-500 was one of the first guitar synthesizers.

name: Roland GR-55
description: The Roland GR-55 combines a digital guitar synthesizer, virtual guitar modeling, and a guitar-to-MIDI interface in a floor unit.  It requires a hexaphonic pickup (e.g., GK-2AH, GK-3, GK-2B, or GK-3B) to track individual strings. Two synthesizer sounds and a modeling sound can be mixed.  It features 910 editable synthesizer sounds comparable to those found in the Juno-Di and Juno-Stage.  A built-in looper is included, and it functions as a USB audio/MIDI interface with audio playback from a USB stick.

name: Roland GR-700
description: The GR-700 is a 6-voice analog guitar synthesizer with a 24-pin connection and MIDI output.  It uses guitars from the GR series (G-202, G-303, G-505, G-707, G-808, or guitars with a GK-1 pickup).  The sound generation is based on the JX-3P, but it's velocity-sensitive.  It features two digitally controlled oscillators (DCOs) per string, a DCF filter, and a DCA amplifier.  It can store 64 patches internally and another 64 on an optional M-16C memory cartridge.  It also functions as a guitar-to-MIDI interface, though with noticeable latency.

It features 64 internal patches and can store 64 more on an optional M-16C memory cartridge, supporting parameter editing via an optional PG-200 programmer or built-in controls. It also functions as a guitar-to-MIDI interface, albeit with notable latency.

description: The GS-500 is a guitar controller for the GR-500 guitar synthesizer.  It lacks a standard guitar output, instead featuring a 24-pin connector for the control cable to the synthesizer. name: Roland GS-500 Guitar Controller
description: The GS-500 is a controller guitar specifically designed for the GR-500 guitar synthesizer. This Les Paul-shaped guitar, constructed with a mahogany body and maple top, was manufactured by Ibanez/Greco (Fuji Gen Gakki) to Roland's specifications. It includes master volume for the pure guitar sound, separate volume and tone controls, a 3-stage equalizer switch, four volume controls with on/off switches for 'Polyensemble', 'Bass', 'Solo-Melody', and 'External-Synthesizer' sections, 'Remote' and 'Portamento' on/off switches, and a three-stage switch for selecting Guitar, Synthesizer, or Dual sound.

name: Roland HS-10
description: The Roland HS-10 is a 6-voice, digitally controlled analog synthesizer. Essentially a cosmetically different version of the Alpha Juno-1, it features 49 non-velocity-sensitive keys and was marketed for home use. The HS-10 is MIDI compatible, can receive velocity data, and shares SysEx compatibility with the Alpha Juno-1, Alpha Juno-2, HS-80, and MKS-50. For easier parameter editing, it can be connected to the PG-300 programmer via MIDI. Each voice features a DCO, a fixed high-pass filter, a dynamic low-pass filter, a dynamic amplifier, an envelope generator, and an LFO. Sounds can be further enhanced with a chorus effect.  It offers 64 non-editable presets and 64 user-programmable sounds.  Some parameter adjustments have a coarse resolution.

The Juno-106 was also sold as the Juno-106S or HS-60 with built-in speakers.

name: Roland JV-1000
description: The JV-1000 is a 28-voice, 8-part multitimbral digital synthesizer with a 76-note velocity-sensitive keyboard with aftertouch, and a built-in sequencer.  It features a slot for a voice expansion board, adding 28 voices with specialized sounds. Its sound engine is identical to the JV-90. A patch consists of up to 4 tones, two of which can be combined using one of 10 structures. Each tone has a PCM oscillator, a 12dB multi-mode filter, a dynamic amplifier, 3 envelopes, and 2 LFOs.  The structure can add a booster and ring modulator.  Velocity and note range limitations allow for split, layer, and crossover sounds within a patch. Performances manage up to 7 parts and a rhythm set. Sounds can be expanded with wave expansion boards and SO-PCM1 cards. The built-in 8-track sequencer with a floppy drive and second display is similar to the MC-50.

name: Roland JV-1000

A patch consists of up to 4 tones, with two tones combined via one of 10 structures. A tone includes a PCM oscillator, 12dB multi-mode filter, dynamic amplifier, 3 envelopes, and 2 LFOs, with additional booster and ring modulator options.  It has an 8-track sequencer with a floppy drive and a second display, similar in functionality to the MC-50. There are 8 internal songs and each track can record data from all 16 MIDI channels.

name: Roland JV-1010
description: The Roland JV-1010 is a 64-voice, 16-part multitimbral rack-mounted synthesizer.  It features wave expansion capabilities via SR-JV80 series boards, one insert MFX, chorus, and reverb.  It requires an editor program for sound design.  Each patch contains up to four tones, each using one of ten structures. Tones consist of a PCM oscillator, a 12dB multi-mode filter, a dynamic amplifier, three envelopes, and two LFOs.  Additional features include a booster and ring modulator (depending on structure), and a 24dB filter Q when two filters are used in the same settings. Velocity and note-based tone limits allow for split, layer, and crossover sounds within a single patch.  It includes ROM samples from the JV-1080 and the Session board. Performances manage up to 15 parts (with patches) and a rhythm set, with freely assignable MIDI channels for each part.

A sound program (patch) consists of up to 4 Tones, two of which can be combined via one of 10 structures. A Tone consists of a PCM oscillator, a 12dB multi-mode filter, a dynamic amplifier, 3 envelopes, and 2 LFOs. Through the choice of structure, boosters and a ring modulator can optionally be added, and with the same setting of two filters, a quality of 24dB can be achieved. Because Tones can be limited in velocity and note range, split, layer, and crossover sounds are possible within a single patch. In addition to the ROM samples of the JV-1080, those of the Session Board are also included. The composition of up to 15 parts (with patches) and one rhythm set is managed by a Performance, with MIDI channels freely selectable for each individual part.

name: Roland JV-1080
description: The JV-1080 is a 64-voice, 16-part multitimbral rack synthesizer module without a keyboard. Its sound library can be expanded with four SR-JV80 series Wave Expansion Boards. It occupies 2U in a 19" rack format and offers 1 insert MFX in addition to chorus and reverb effects. A sound program (Patch) consists of up to 4 Tones, two of which can be combined via one of 10 Structures. A Tone comprises a PCM oscillator, a 12dB multi-mode filter, a dynamic amplifier, 3 envelopes, and 2 LFOs. Depending on the chosen structure, a booster and ring modulator can be added, and with identical settings for two filters, a 24dB slope can be achieved. By limiting Tones in terms of velocity and note range, split, layer, and crossover sounds are possible within a single patch. The ROM sample library has been significantly expanded compared to its predecessors. The combination of up to 15 parts (with patches) and one rhythm set is managed by a Performance, with MIDI channels freely assignable for each individual part.

name: Roland JV-1080
description: The Roland JV-1080 is a 64-voice, 16-part multitimbral rack synthesizer.  Its sound library can be expanded with four SR-JV80 wave expansion boards.  It offers PCM oscillators, multimode filters, dynamic amplifiers, and multiple envelopes and LFOs.  It supports various sound layering and splitting techniques within a single patch.

name: Roland JV-2080
description: The JV-2080 is a 64-voice, 16-part multitimbral rack synthesizer without a keyboard.  Its sound library can be expanded with eight SR-JV80 series wave expansion boards. It offers 3 insert effects in addition to chorus and reverb. A sound program (patch) consists of up to 4 tones, two of which can be combined via one of 10 structures.

name: Roland JV-30
description: The Roland JV-30 is a 24-voice, 16-part multitimbral, GS-compatible digital synthesizer with 61 velocity-sensitive keys.  Its sound generation is based on the SoundCanvas SC-55 module and offers only limited sound editing capabilities.

name: Roland JV-30 Synthesizer
description: The JV-30 is a 24-voice, 16-part multitimbral, GS-compatible digital synthesizer with 61 velocity-sensitive keys.  Sound generation is based on the SoundCanvas SC-55 module, offering limited sound modification options.

name: Roland JV-35
description: The JV-35 is a 28-voice, 16-part multitimbral, GS-compatible digital synthesizer with 61 velocity-sensitive keys.  Its sound generation is based on the Sound Canvas SC-55MKII module.  While sounds cannot be created from scratch, users can modify existing tones and save them as new "Tones." It features a slot for a Voice Expansion Board to add more sounds.
keywords: Sound Canvas SC-55MKII based sound generation

name: Roland JV-50
description: The JV-50 is a 28-voice, 16-part multitimbral, GS-compatible digital synthesizer with 61 velocity-sensitive keys and a sequencer for SMF files.  Sound generation is based on the SoundCanvas SC-55MKII module.  While sounds cannot be fully programmed, users can modify certain parameters.  The JV-50 is identical to the JV-35 except for the sequencer and has space for a voice expansion board that can add 28 more voices with either GS or JV sounds.

name: Roland JV-80
description: The JV-80 is a 28-voice, 8-part multitimbral digital synthesizer with 61 velocity-sensitive keys and aftertouch. A sound program (patch) consists of up to 4 tones, two of which can be combined using one of 10 structures. A tone consists of a PCM oscillator, 12dB multi-mode filter, dynamic amplifier, 3 envelopes, and 2 LFOs. Depending on the structure, booster and ring modulator options are available, and using identical filter settings achieves 24dB resonance.  Velocity and note range limitations allow for split, layer, and crossover sounds within a single patch. Up to 7 parts (with patches) and a rhythm set are controlled by a performance. The sound library can be expanded with a wave expansion board.
keywords: Booster and ring modulator (depending on structure)

name: Roland JV-880
description: The JV-880 is a 28-voice, 8-part multitimbral digital synthesizer module. A sound program (Patch) consists of up to 4 Tones, two of which can be combined via one of 10 Structures. A Tone comprises a PCM oscillator, a 12dB multi-mode filter, a dynamic amplifier, 3 envelopes, and 2 LFOs. Depending on the chosen structure, a booster and ring modulator can be added, and with identical settings for two filters, a 24dB slope can be achieved. By limiting Tones in terms of velocity and note range, split, layer, and crossover sounds are possible within a single patch. The combination of up to 7 parts (with patches) and one rhythm set is managed by a Performance. The JV-880's sound library can be expanded with a Wave Expansion Board, providing additional PCM samples to the oscillators. The JV-880 is the module counterpart to the JV-80.
keywords: Patch consists of up to 4 Tones
PCM oscillator, 12dB multi-mode filter, dynamic amplifier, 3 envelopes, and 2 LFOs per Tone

Performance mode for up to 7 parts and 1 rhythm set

name: Roland JV-880
description: The JV-880 is a 28-voice, 8-part multitimbral digital synthesizer module.  A sound program (patch) consists of up to 4 tones, two of which can be combined using one of 10 structures. A tone consists of a PCM oscillator, a 12dB multi-mode filter, a dynamic amplifier, 3 envelopes, and 2 LFOs.  The sound library can be expanded with a wave expansion board.

name: Roland JV-90 Expandable Synthesizer
description: The JV-90 is a 28-voice, 8-part multitimbral digital synthesizer with 76 velocity-sensitive keys and aftertouch.  It features a slot for a voice expansion board, allowing for the addition of 28 voices with specialized sounds.  A JV-90 patch can consist of up to 4 tones, each using one of 10 structures. Each tone includes a PCM oscillator, filter, amplifier, envelopes, and LFOs.  The sound library can be expanded with wave expansion boards and PCM cards.

name: Roland JW-50
description: The JW-50 is a 24-voice, 16-part multitimbral, GS-compatible digital synthesizer with 61 velocity-sensitive keys and aftertouch.  It includes a built-in SMF sequencer with a floppy disk drive, capable of recording 8 internal songs and featuring a backing function with 30 styles.  Sound generation is similar to the SC-55 module, with minor sound adjustments available (vibrato rate/intensity/delay, filter resonance/cutoff, and amp attack/decay/release).  Effects include chorus and reverb, and 8 sliders control parameters including part volumes.

name: Roland JW-50 MIDI-Workstation
description: The JW-50 is a 24-voice, 16-part multitimbral, GS-compatible digital synthesizer with 61 velocity-sensitive keys and aftertouch. It features a built-in SMF sequencer with a (DD) floppy drive, capable of recording 8 internal songs and offering a backing function with 30 styles. The sound generation is roughly equivalent to the SC-55 module, and sounds can only be slightly altered (Vibrato Rate/Depth/Delay, Filter Resonance/Cutoff, and Amp Attack/Decay/Release). Chorus and Reverb effects are on board, and 8 faders can be used to control part volumes, among other things.
keywords: Built-in SMF sequencer with (DD) floppy drive
Sound generation similar to SC-55 module
Limited sound editing (Vibrato Rate/Depth/Delay, Filter Resonance/Cutoff, Amp Attack/Decay/Release)

name: Roland JX-1
description: The JX-1 is a 24-voice digital synthesizer with 61 velocity-sensitive keys.  Sound generation is based on PCM samples, processed through a dynamic filter and amplifier. Chorus and reverb effects are available.  It has 64 presets, and 32 altered sounds can be saved, but only a few parameters (cutoff, color, attack, release, vibrato depth and rate, chorus/reverb on/off) are editable.  It's neither GS nor GM compatible, nor multitimbral.

name: Roland JX-10
description: The JX-10 is a 12-voice, digitally controlled analog synthesizer with 76 velocity-sensitive keys and channel aftertouch. Essentially a double JX-8P, it's 2-part multitimbral (Upper and Lower). Each voice features 2 DCOs (without pulse width modulation but with cross modulation), 1 resonant DCF, 1 dynamic DCA, 2 envelopes, and 1 LFO. The VCA can be switched to gate mode.  It can operate on two independently selectable MIDI channels and can be programmed via the optional PG-800 programmer. The M-64C cartridge expands sound storage. A small, non-editable sequencer can record notes, program changes, hold, and portamento data to an M-16C or cartridge.

name: Roland JX-10 SUPER JX Polyphonic MIDI Synthesizer
description: The JX-10 is a 12-voice, digitally controlled analog synthesizer with 76 velocity-sensitive keys and channel aftertouch. In principle, it is a double JX-8P, meaning it is 2-part multitimbral (Upper and Lower). Per voice, it features 2 DCOs without pulse width but with cross-modulation, 1 resonant DCF, and 1 DCA, both dynamic, 2 envelopes, and 1 LFO. The VCA could be switched to Gate mode. The JX-10 can operate on two differently settable MIDI channels, and for programming, the separately available PG-800 programmer can be connected (not simultaneously with MIDI). For storing additional sounds, the M-64C cartridge can be inserted. A small, non-editable sequencer can record notes, program changes, hold, and portamento data on an M-16C (400 events) or cartridge (1600 events).
keywords: Roland JX-10 SUPER JX Polyphonic MIDI Synthesizer
Per voice: 2 DCOs (Digitally Controlled Oscillators) with cross-modulation
