name: Roland JX-305
description: The Roland JX-305 is a groove synthesizer combining an 8-part multitimbral digital synthesizer with a pattern sequencer. It has a 61-key velocity-sensitive keyboard. Essentially a keyboard version of the MC-505 Groovebox, it shares the same preset patterns and sounds.  Sound generation is based on the 4-tone, 10-structure architecture of the JV/XP series, but with ROM samples replaced by dance-oriented sounds. The sequencer is pattern-based, with 8 tracks fixed to parts (and MIDI channels 1-7 and 10). During playback, tracks can be individually muted, and the MEGAMIX function lets you swap tracks from the current pattern with those from other patterns.  An arpeggiator and RPS sequencer can be used additionally.

name: Roland JX-305 Groove Synthesizer
description: The JX-305 Groove Synthesizer combines an 8-part multitimbral digital synthesizer with a pattern sequencer and has a velocity-sensitive 61-key keyboard.  It's essentially the keyboard version of the MC-505 Groovebox and has the same preset patterns and sounds.  The sound generation is based on the 4 Tone/10 Structure architecture of the JV/XP series, with the ROM samples exchanged for dance-oriented sounds.  The sequencer is pattern-based, with the 8 tracks permanently assigned to the parts (and MIDI channels 1 to 7 and 10).  During playback, the tracks can be individually muted via buttons, and the MEGAMIX function allows you to exchange the tracks of the running pattern with those of other patterns.  An arpeggiator and RPS sequencer can also be used alternatively.

name: Roland JX-3P
description: The JX-3P is a 6-voice, digitally controlled analog synthesizer with 61 non-velocity-sensitive keys, a 128-step sequencer, 32 preset and 32 user sounds. Each voice has two DCOs, a resonant VCF, a dynamic VCA, a static high-pass filter, one envelope generator, and one LFO. The VCA can be switched to gate mode.  Oscillators produce square, sawtooth, and pulse waves; the second can also produce noise. Hard-sync and a "metal" effect (a type of cross-modulation) add sound variety.  It is an early MIDI synthesizer and only works in Omni mode by default. Data could be saved to tape, and the optional PG-200 programmer could be used for programming.

name: Roland JX-8P
description: The JX-8P is a 6-voice, digitally controlled analog synthesizer with 61 velocity-sensitive keys, 32 preset and 32 user sounds. Per voice, it offers 2 DCOs without pulse width modulation but with cross-modulation, 1 resonant DCF and 1 DCA (both dynamic), 2 envelopes, and 1 LFO; the VCA could be switched to Gate. The JX-8P can operate in Omni mode or with an adjustable MIDI channel, and for programming, the separately available PG-800 programmer could be connected as an alternative (not simultaneously with MIDI).
keywords: Per voice: 2 DCOs (with cross-modulation, no PWM), 1 resonant DCF (dynamically controlled filter), 1 dynamic DCA (amplifier), 2 envelopes, 1 LFO
External programmer support (Roland PG-800, not simultaneous with MIDI)

name: Roland JX-8P
description: The JX-8P is a 6-voice, digitally controlled analog synthesizer with 61 velocity-sensitive keys, 32 preset and 32 user sounds. Each voice features 2 DCOs (without pulse width modulation but with cross modulation), 1 resonant DCF, 1 dynamic DCA, 2 envelopes, and 1 LFO; the VCA could be switched to gate mode.  It operates in Omni mode or with a selectable MIDI channel. For programming, the separately available PG-800 programmer could be connected (not simultaneously with MIDI).

name: Roland Juno-106
description: The Juno-106 is a 6-voice analog synthesizer with 61 keys. Each voice includes an oscillator (DCO), high-pass filter, dynamic low-pass filter, dynamic amplifier, and an envelope generator.  It features 128 memory locations organized into two groups of eight banks with eight sound programs each. Sounds can also be stored and loaded from tape.  The Juno-106 has a MIDI interface and transmits both note and parameter data via SysEx, allowing it to send all necessary parameters to a second Juno-106 (or sequencer) when switching sound programs.

name: Roland Juno-106
description: The Juno-106 is a 6-voice analog synthesizer with 61 keys.  Each voice features a DCO (Digitally Controlled Oscillator), high-pass filter, dynamic low-pass filter, dynamic amplifier, and envelope generator.  It's similar to the Juno-60 but offers expanded memory (128 patches vs. 56) organized into two groups of eight banks with eight programs each.  Patches can be saved and loaded from tape.  It also includes a MIDI interface for transmitting notes and parameter values via SysEx.

name: Roland Juno-6
description: The Juno-6 is a 6-voice analog synthesizer with 61 keys and an arpeggiator. Each voice has one DCO, a high-pass filter, a dynamic low-pass filter, a dynamic amplifier, and an envelope generator.  Sound programs are not savable. It includes headphone and main outputs (L/Mono, R), and inputs for a sustain pedal, arpeggio clock, and filter cutoff control.

name: Roland Juno-6
description: The Juno-6 is a 6-voice analog synthesizer with 61 keys and an arpeggiator. Each voice has one DCO (Digitally Controlled Oscillator), a high-pass filter, a dynamic low-pass filter, a dynamic amplifier, and an envelope generator.  Sounds are not savable as programs.

name: Roland Juno-60
description: The Juno-60 is a digitally controlled, 6-voice analog synthesizer with 61 keys and an arpeggiator. Each voice has an oscillator (DCO), high-pass filter, dynamic low-pass filter, dynamic amplifier, and envelope generator. It can store 56 sounds and allows data storage and loading via tape.  It also features a DCB port for data exchange between synthesizers.

name: Roland Juno-60
description: The Juno-60 is a digitally controlled, 6-voice analog synthesizer with 61 keys and an arpeggiator. Each voice has an oscillator (DCO), high-pass filter, dynamic low-pass filter, dynamic amplifier, and an envelope.  It can store 56 sounds which can also be saved to and loaded from tape. It has a DCB connection for exchanging data with other synthesizers.

name: Roland Juno-D
description: The Juno-D is a 16-part multitimbral, 64-voice digital synthesizer with 61 velocity-sensitive keys and an arpeggiator. Sound generation and operation are similar to the RS-50, with two tones forming a patch as a split or layer.  While tones can't be fully edited, some parameters are adjustable. The internal PCM samples are completely revised.

description: The Roland MC-303 is a pioneering synthesizer groove box, an all-in-one electronic music production workstation. It combines a sound module, a drum machine, and a sequencer in one compact unit, designed for creating electronic dance music. It offers a wide range of preset patterns and sounds, allowing users to quickly create tracks without needing additional equipment. It lacks the MC-505's Megamix mode and has 4 rotary encoders instead of 8 sliders for part control.  It features a turntable emulation controller for quick tempo and pitch changes.

name: Roland MC-307 GrooveBox

The sound generation principle is based on the 4 Tone-10 Structure architecture of the JV/XP series, with ROM samples exchanged for dance-ready sounds. Parameters are fully compatible with the MC-505, but the MC-307 has an additional bank of PCM samples and newer, fresher preset patterns and patches as a basis for creating your own grooves. However, the MC-307 does not have a Megamix mode and only 4 rotary encoders instead of the 8 sliders on the MC-505 for controlling parts. Tempo changes like record scratching, or just pitch and tempo changes, can be quickly controlled with the Turntable Emulation knob.

name: Roland MC-4A
description: The MC-4 is a digital sequencer for CV/Gate signals with 4 independent tracks. Sequences can be programmed step-by-step or played in using a CV/Gate keyboard. Two-stage input (first pitch, then step length) is also possible. All entries can be edited on the MC-4, though users need to familiarize themselves with the specific display on the 15-character screen. Each track provides two control voltages (CV-1 and CV-2), a Gate signal, and an 'MPX' trigger signal (e.g., for portamento), allowing control of a connected synthesizer's pitch, dynamics, or filter. The MC-4 features a built-in DIN-SYNC jack and can function as a synchronization master or slave for other DIN-SYNC equipped devices such as the CSQ-600, CR-8000, TB-303, MC-202, TR-606, and TR-808. Through its TAPE SYNC connections, the MC-4 can also output an FSK signal for recording onto magnetic tape, enabling synchronous playback later. Additionally, tempo can be externally controlled via a control voltage. Programmed sequences must be saved to tape or a cassette recorder before powering off if they are to be used again. Accordingly, functions for saving, loading, and verifying data on external audio recording devices are available. The MC-4A was delivered with 16KB of internal memory for approximately 3700 notes/events and could be upgraded to a full MC-4B (which featured 48KB for approximately 11500 notes/events and an interface for the MTR-100 data cassette recorder) using the OM-4 upgrade kit.

name: Roland MC-4B
description: The MC-4B is a digital CV/Gate sequencer with 4 independent tracks.  Sequences can be programmed step-by-step or played in using a CV/Gate keyboard.  It offers two-stage input (pitch, then step width) and allows editing of all entries. Each track has two control voltages (CV-1 and CV-2), gate, and a trigger signal ("MPX") for controlling aspects like portamento or filter on a connected synthesizer. It features DIN-SYNC and tape sync capabilities for synchronization with other devices. Data must be saved to tape before power down. The MC-4B had 48kB of internal memory (compared to 16kB in the MC-4A).

name: Roland MC-4B Micro-Composer
description: The MC-4 is a digital sequencer for CV/Gate signals with 4 independent tracks. Sequences can be programmed step-by-step or played in using a CV/Gate keyboard. Two-stage input (first pitches, then step length) is also possible. All entries can be edited on the MC-4, though one must get used to a special display on the 15-character screen. Per track, two control voltages (CV-1 and CV-2), Gate, and an "MPX" trigger signal for e.g., portamento, are available, allowing control over not only pitch but also dynamics or the filter of an connected synthesizer. The MC-4 has a built-in DIN-SYNC socket and can serve as a synchronization master or slave for other DIN-SYNC equipped devices. Via the TAPE SYNC connections, the MC-4 can also output an FSK signal, which can be recorded on a tape and later allow the MC-4 to run synchronously. Furthermore, the tempo can be controlled externally via a control voltage. Entered sequences must be saved to tape or cassette recorder before disconnecting power if they are to be used again. Accordingly, functions for saving, loading, and verifying data on external audio recording devices are available. The MC-4B features 48kB internal memory for approximately 11500 notes/events and an interface for the MTR-100 data cassette recorder.

name: Roland MC-50
description: The MC-50 is a compact, song-oriented MIDI sequencer with two independent MIDI outputs, a 3.5" floppy drive, and a backlit display.  Unlike its predecessors, the operating system is integrated, not loaded from disk.  It includes an 8-track sequencer and a performance package program. However, it cannot directly handle standard MIDI files (SMF) or bulk dumps from other devices; alternative operating systems can be loaded from disk for this (MRB-500 Bulk Librarian or MRM-500 SMF-Converter).  In normal operation, it's an 8-track sequencer, with each track recording all 16 MIDI channels.  There's an additional rhythm track for up to 240 rhythm patterns with up to 32 notes each.  Up to 8 songs can be stored. The MC-50 can be synchronized internally or externally via MIDI clock signals and a FSK signal (Tape Sync).

name: Roland MC-500
description: The MC-500 is a song-oriented MIDI sequencer with two independent MIDI outputs and a 3.5" floppy disk drive. Its operating system loads from disk.  It features a number pad, function buttons, cursor keys, a data entry wheel, and track buttons. It initially came with MRC-500 software for 4-track sequencing (16 MIDI channels per track), a tempo track, and a rhythm track with up to 90 patterns.  The MC-500 could store up to 8 songs depending on memory.  The S-MRC software upgrades it to 8 tracks and 240 patterns. Additional software offered expanded functionality.

name: Roland MC-500MKII
description: The MC-500MKII is a song-oriented MIDI sequencer with two independent MIDI outputs and a 3.5" floppy drive.  Its operating system is initially loaded from a diskette.  It features a ten-key numeric keypad and other design elements reminiscent of a calculator.  It includes 6 drive buttons, 7 function buttons, 2 cursor buttons, a value input wheel (Alpha-Dial), and 5 illuminated track buttons, along with a 2-line display (not backlit). It was shipped with S-MRC software, turning it into an 8-track sequencer capable of recording all 16 MIDI channels on each track.  Additional features include a tempo track and a rhythm track for up to 240 rhythm patterns.

name: Roland MC-500MKII Micro Composer with 3.5" Floppy
description: The MC-500MKII is a song-oriented MIDI sequencer with 2 independent MIDI outputs and a 3.5" floppy drive, whose operating system must be loaded from a floppy disk at startup. The hardware, with its numeric keypad and design, resembles a calculating machine and offers excellent operability. It features 6 drive buttons, 7 function buttons, 2 cursor buttons, an Alpha-Dial for value input, 5 illuminated track buttons, and an unfortunately non-backlit 2-line display. The MC-500MKII was delivered with the S-MRC software, enabling it to function as an 8-track sequencer, where all 16 MIDI channels can be recorded on each track. A tempo track and a rhythm track are also available, allowing up to 240 rhythm patterns, each with up to 32 different note numbers, to be arranged. Users can create their own patterns. The MC-500MKII can store up to 8 songs in memory, provided the maximum memory space of 100,000 events is sufficient. All entries (events) can be fully edited using the Microscop function. Unfortunately, constantly inserting the system floppy for various functions can be annoying. The MC-500MKII can also be started with other operating systems, such as the Performance Package Super-MRP for creating stage-ready song sequences, the Rhythm Bank MRD-500 for pre-programmed patterns, or the Bulk Librarian MRB-500 for managing bulk dumps. Since the S-MRC software does not natively support Standard MIDI Files (SMF), the MRM-500 software was available for converting S-MRC songs to SMFs and vice versa. The MC-500MKII differs from its predecessor mainly by its larger memory. Songs and operating systems can be loaded alternately from MC-500 and MKII. It synchronizes internally or externally via MIDI Clock or FSK (Tape Sync) signals.

name: Roland MC-8 Micro Composer
description: The Roland MC-8 Micro Composer is a computer-controlled 8-channel CV/Gate sequencer and the first fully editable sequencer ever. The MC-8 consists of two hardware components: the control computer with input buttons and the connection panel, which are connected by a thick multi-pin cable. Each channel provides a control voltage (CV) and a gate signal. Additionally, a total of 6 outputs labeled MPX can be set to high level or 0 to trigger various functions. Sequences can be entered via CV/Gate input from an external keyboard or in a rather cryptic way using the numeric keypad. For saving sequences, the MC-8 has a tape interface (IN and OUT). The FSK signal can now be recorded with an HD recorder instead of a tape/cassette recorder. The MC-8 can also be externally synchronized via the FSK signal.

name: Roland MKB-1000
description: The MKB-1000 is a 2-zone MIDI master keyboard with 88 weighted, velocity-sensitive wooden keys and channel aftertouch. Each zone (UPPER and LOWER) has buttons to increase/decrease the MIDI channel, displayed on a 7-segment display. MIDI data is output via four parallel MIDI OUT jacks, with incoming data merged via MIDI IN. A MIDI THRU jack is also present.  Its functionality is identical to the MKB-300, except the MKB-300 uses 76 plastic keys.

name: Roland MKB-1000 MIDI Master Keyboard
description: The MKB-1000 is a 2-zone MIDI master keyboard with 88 weighted, velocity-sensitive wooden keys and channel aftertouch. Each zone, called UPPER and LOWER, has two buttons to increase or decrease the MIDI channel, displayed on a 7-segment display.  The MKB-1000 can operate in WHOLE, SPLIT, or DUAL mode. Program changes can be generated manually or saved as a patch along with the mode for each zone, which are then sent when recalled. 128 patches can be stored internally or on an M-64C cartridge. The MKB-1000 outputs playing data via four parallel MIDI OUT sockets, merging incoming data from the MIDI IN socket. A MIDI THRU socket is also provided for exclusively forwarding MIDI IN data.  The MKB-1000's functions are identical to the MKB-300, which has 76 plastic keys. The MKB-1000 and MKB-300 were the first dedicated master keyboards, separating MIDI data generation from sound generation and forming a foundation with the MKS-10, MKS-30, and MKS-80 modules.

name: Roland MKB-1000 MIDI Master Keyboard, 88-keys

It allows for independent control of two zones, 'UPPER' and 'LOWER', each with dedicated buttons to adjust and display the MIDI channel on a 7-segment display for clear oversight. The keyboard supports WHOLE, SPLIT, or DUAL modes. Users can manually generate program changes or save them as patches along with the zone modes, to be sent upon recall. It offers 128 patch memories, storable internally or on an M-64C Cartridge. The MKB-1000 outputs playing data through four parallel MIDI OUT jacks and features a MIDI IN jack with a merge function, allowing incoming MIDI data to be combined with performance data. A separate MIDI THRU jack is also provided for direct forwarding of MIDI IN data. The MKB-1000, along with the MKB-300, were among the first dedicated master keyboards, marking the beginning of the separation between MIDI data control and sound generation, often paired with modules like MKS-10, MKS-30, and MKS-80.

name: Roland MKS-100
description: The Roland MKS-100 is an 8-voice rackmount sampler module with a built-in 2.8" Quick Disk drive. It samples at 12-bit resolution with either a 15kHz or 30kHz sampling rate. The 256kB of internal memory is divided into four banks of 64kB each, providing a maximum total sampling time of 4.4 seconds (approximately 1.1 seconds per bank). Two banks can be combined for longer samples.  The MKS-100 allows for sample editing, looping, and the application of dynamic envelopes, but lacks a dynamic filter. In MIDI Poly mode, up to four samples can be split across the keyboard or layered (note range 24 to 104).  In Mono mode, the samples can be accessed on four consecutive MIDI channels. Unlike its larger counterparts (S-50, S-330), the MKS-100 doesn't support monitor or mouse control and relies solely on its front panel controls and single-line display.

name: Roland MKS-100

Its 256kB internal memory is divided into four 64kB banks, allowing for a total sample time of 4.4 seconds (approximately 1.1 seconds per bank). Longer samples can be created by combining two banks. Samples can be edited, equipped with a dynamic envelope, and looped; however, there's no dynamic filter. Up to four samples can be used simultaneously, either split or layered across the note range (C2-C7) in MIDI poly mode. In mono mode, the samples can be addressed on four consecutive channels.  Unlike the Roland S-50 and S-330, it does not feature mouse or monitor operation.

name: Roland MKS-7
description: The Roland MKS-7 Super Quartet is a multitimbral analog synthesizer module with PCM rhythm sounds. It has four sections: a monophonic bass section, a two-voice melody section, a four-voice chord section, and a rhythm section with 11 drum sounds based on the TR-707.  Sound editing is primarily done via MIDI SysEx data using external editors.

name: Roland MKS-7 MIDI Sound Module Super-Quartet
description: The MKS-7 SUPER QUARTET is a multi-timbral, analog synthesizer module in a 19-inch, 2U rack format with PCM rhythm sounds. It features 4 sections: a monophonic BASS section with 20 sounds, a 2-voice MELODY section, and a 4-voice CHORD section, each with 100 sounds. The rhythm section, fixed to MIDI channel 10, offers 11 unchangeable drum sounds (PCM samples): BD, SN, HiT, MiT, LoT, CH, OH, Clap, Rim, Ride, Crash, which correspond to those of the TR-707. The note numbers are fixed. The sound generation of the three melodic sections is equivalent to that of the Juno-106, meaning each voice has one oscillator (DCO), a high-pass filter, a dynamic low-pass filter, a dynamic amp, and an envelope. Editing sounds on the device itself is only possible in a special engineering mode; however, existing sounds can be modified via MIDI SysEx data, for example, with a Juno-106 (editor) or HS-60. The MKS-7 is the first (more than 2-part) multi-timbral MIDI synthesizer with drum sounds. The MKS-7 can also be put into a WHOLE mode, where only the CHORD part is active, but with 6 voices, essentially a Juno-106 in a rack format.

name: Roland MKS-70
description: The Roland MKS-70 Super JX is a 12-voice, MIDI-controlled, analog synthesizer module in a 19-inch rack format.  Each voice has two digitally controlled oscillators (DCOs), a non-dynamic high-pass filter, a dynamic 24db low-pass filter, an LFO, and two envelopes. Both DCOs offer sawtooth, square/pulse (variable pulse width), and noise waveforms, can be tuned in semitone steps from 16' to 2', detuned, and hard-synced.  A unique feature is the pitch spread for one oscillator adjustable below 100%. The low-pass filter is resonant, and the envelopes respond to both velocity and key follow. The MKS-70 is the rack version of the JX-10.  It stores 50 preset tones and 50 user tones.  It's 2-part multitimbral, allowing two tones to be combined as split or dual, forming a patch which saves the octave, bend behavior, play mode (solo, unison, polyphonic), and volume balance. It has 64 internal patch memories. An M-64C cartridge doubles the memory.  While it can be edited via MIDI SysEx, a full dump is not possible.  The PG-800 programmer is recommended for easier sound design.

name: Roland MKS-70
description: The SUPER JX MKS-70 is a 12-voice, MIDI-controlled analog synthesizer module in a 19-inch rack format.  Each voice has two digitally controlled oscillators (DCOs), a non-dynamic high-pass filter, a dynamic 24dB low-pass filter, an LFO, and two envelopes. The DCOs offer sawtooth, rectangular/pulse (variable pulse width), and noise waveforms.  It's notable for its ability to adjust the pitch spread of one oscillator to below 100%. The low-pass filter is resonant, and the envelopes respond to both velocity and keyboard position (key follow). It's the rack version of the JX-10, offering 50 preset and 50 user-programmable tones. It's 2-part multitimbral, allowing split or dual combinations.  A M-64C cartridge doubles the internal memory.

name: Roland MKS-80 Super Jupiter
description: An 8-voice, MIDI-controlled, analog synthesizer module in a 19-inch rack format. Each voice has two oscillators, a high-pass filter, a 24dB low-pass filter, an LFO, and two envelopes.  It offers 64 internal tone and patch memories, expandable via M-64C cartridge.
keywords: LFO and two envelopes per voice

name: Roland MKS-80 Synthesizer Module SUPER JUPITER
description: The SUPER JUPITER MKS-80 is an 8-voice, MIDI-controlled, analog synthesizer module in a 19-inch, 2U rack format. Each voice features two oscillators, a non-dynamic high-pass filter, a dynamic 24db low-pass filter, an LFO, and two envelopes. Both oscillators provide triangle, sawtooth, and square/pulse waves (variable pulse width), can be tuned semitone-wise from 32-foot to 2-foot settings, detuned against each other, and hard-synced. OSC2 also offers white noise and "Low" and "High" tunings. A unique feature allows the pitch spread of one oscillator to be set below 100%. The low-pass filter is resonant, and the envelopes react to both velocity and keyboard position (Key Follow). The MKS-80 largely corresponds to the architecture of the Jupiter-8. A single sound program is called a "Tone," with 64 internal storage slots. The MKS-80 is 2-part multitimbral, allowing two Tones to be combined as a Split or DUAL. A combination is called a "Patch," which stores the octave range, bend behavior, playing mode (Solo, Unison, Polyphonic) of the Tones, and their volume balance. There are also 64 internal patch memory slots. An external M-64C cartridge can be inserted to provide an additional 64 Tones and 64 Patches. Furthermore, the MKS-80 can be edited via MIDI SysEx commands, although a complete dump is not possible. Since creating sounds on the MKS-80 by selecting parameter numbers and then entering values via buttons is cumbersome, the MPG-80 Programmer can be connected, which has dedicated controls for all relevant parameters. There were two versions of the MKS-80, which sound different: up to serial number 511799, the well-known Curtis chips (also used in SCI or Oberheim) were employed, after which Roland's own chips and filters were used. The three MKS modules MKS-30 (Planet-S), MKS-10 (Planet-P), and MKS-80 (SUPER JUPITER) were among the first MIDI sound modules ever and, together with the master keyboards MKB-1000 and MKB-300, marked the beginning of the separation of MIDI data and sound generation.

name: Roland MKS-900
description: The Roland MKS-900 MIDI Signal Indicator is a rack-mounted (1U) LED display showing MIDI note data.  It displays the full 88-note piano range (A1 to C8), providing visual monitoring of MIDI messages such as note on/off, program change, and sustain pedal.  It has a MIDI input and 5 parallel MIDI OUT connections, functioning as a MIDI filter and/or THRU box.
keywords: Visual monitoring of note on/off, program change, and sustain pedal

name: Roland MKS-900 MIDI Signal Indicator
description: The Roland MKS-900 MIDI SIGNAL INDICATOR is a 1U rack-mount LED display visually arranged like a keyboard for MIDI note data. The MKS-900 displays the full note range of an 88-key piano (A1 to C8). This allows for easy monitoring of MIDI messages such as note on/off, program changes, and sustain pedal. The MKS-900 has one MIDI input and 5 parallel MIDI OUT connections. In addition to its valuable monitoring function, the MKS-900 allows choosing whether all data or only the data of a single, adjustable MIDI channel is output via MIDI OUT. The MKS-900 can therefore also serve as a MIDI filter and/or THRU box.

name: Roland MPG-80
description: The MPG-80 is a programmer for the MKS-80 sound module. It can function as a tabletop unit or be rack-mounted (4U).  It features sliders (31), rotary knobs (10), slide switches (20), and rotary switches (3) corresponding to parameters, allowing for quick and easy sound creation with an analog-style interface.  It has MIDI IN, MIDI THRU, and a 6-pin DIN programmer OUT. Connection to the MKS-80 is via a 6-pin DIN cable, which provides power and data transfer.

name: Roland MPG-80 Programmer for SUPER JUPITER MKS-80
description: The MPG-80 is a programmer for the MKS-80 sound module, designed for tabletop use or 19-inch rack mounting (occupying 4U). It features 31 sliders, 10 rotary knobs, 20 slide switches, and 3 rotary switches that correspond to the parameters of the MKS-80, allowing for quick and convenient sound creation with an 'analog' control surface. The MPG-80 has a MIDI IN, a MIDI THRU, and a 6-pin DIN Programmer OUT connection. The MPG-80 is connected to the MKS-80 via a 6-pin DIN cable, which transmits all data and simultaneously powers the MPG-80. A controlling keyboard or sequencer can be connected to the MPG-80's MIDI IN, and its data is merged with the data from the programmer and sent to the MKS-80. This is practical as it avoids having to switch the MKS-80 between MIDI control and programmer operation, which would otherwise deactivate its MIDI IN port. The MPG-80 sends its data, i.e., control movements, as MIDI SysEx messages. Only the MIDI data present at MIDI IN is forwarded via MIDI THRU.

name: Roland MPU-101
description: The Roland MPU-101 is a MIDI-to-CV interface with CV, dynamics, and gate outputs for four channels, plus four additional control outputs.  It's capable of operating in Time Code mode, sending MIDI clock-synchronized trigger impulses for use with older equipment.

name: Roland MPU-103
description: The MPU-103 is a MIDI channel filter and converter in a 1/2 19" rack case. It features MIDI IN, OUT, and THRU connections.  The incoming MIDI signal at MIDI IN is passed through to THRU unchanged.  MIDI OUT transmits data from a freely selectable MIDI channel, which can be either maintained or converted to another channel using the converter switch. LEDs indicate power and MIDI data reception.

name: Roland MPU-103
description: The MPU-103 is a MIDI channel filter and converter.  It allows selection of a specific MIDI channel to pass through, and also the conversion of the selected channel to a different channel.  It features MIDI IN, OUT, and THRU connections. The unit is housed in a 1/2 19" rack case.
keywords: MIDI IN, OUT, and THRU connections

name: Roland MPU-103 MIDI Channel Filter/Converter
description: The MPU-103 is a MIDI channel filter and converter housed in a 1/2 19-inch rackmount case, featuring MIDI IN, OUT, and THRU connections on the rear. The signal arriving at MIDI IN is output unchanged at THRU. At MIDI OUT, data from a freely selected MIDI channel (chosen with the FILTER rotary switch) is output. The channel number can be retained or remapped to any other using the CONVERTER rotary switch. A red LED indicates power supply (via PSA-series AC adapter), and a green LED indicates the arrival of MIDI data. The MPU-103 was originally intended to be called MI-30 but was only released under the name MPU-103.
keywords: FILTER rotary switch for channel selection

name: Roland MSQ-700 Digital MIDI-Keyboard Recorder (DCB & MIDI)
description: The MSQ-700 is an 8-track MIDI sequencer, capable of recording data from all 16 MIDI channels on each track. Notes can be recorded via real-time input or step-by-step entry, and overdubs are possible (e.g., to record data from other MIDI channels in subsequent passes). The MSQ-700 is song-oriented, meaning it does not feature patterns (reusable song sections). The MSQ-700 lacks detailed editing functions, but multiple tracks can be merged into one (Merge function), and the playback order of tracks can be determined using the Chain function. In total, approximately 6500 events can be recorded, making the MSQ-700 the 'big brother' of the MSQ-100 and a successor to the CSQ-600. The MSQ-700 can operate as a master or slave, via MIDI or DIN SYNC, as well as to an FSK signal, which the MSQ-700 can also generate. Data can be saved to tape/cassette recorder (using an FSK signal, which can nowadays also be recorded with an HD recorder).

name: Roland MT-100
description: The MT-100 is a song-oriented 4 (5)-track MIDI sequencer featuring a built-in MT-32 sound generator, housed in a console-style enclosure. Its sequencer tracks are divided into two main tracks, two sub-tracks, and one rhythm track, with recording possible only on the main tracks. Data from all MIDI channels can be recorded simultaneously on each main track, with merge/bounce functionality. The sound generation is equivalent to the MT-32 module, offering 8 melody parts and one rhythm part. It is 32-voice polyphonic, with 128 tones plus 34 rhythm instruments, and includes reverb. Sequencer data is volatile (lost on power-off) but can be saved and loaded from a Quick Disk (2.8'' disk). While it records note and CC data, it does not record SysEx data.

name: Roland MT-100
description: The MT-100 is a song-oriented 4 (or 5 with rhythm track) track MIDI sequencer with integrated MT-32 sound generation in a console-style housing.  It has 2 main and 2 sub tracks (plus a rhythm track), recording is only possible on the main tracks.  All MIDI channels can be recorded simultaneously on each main track and merged later. Data from main and sub tracks can be exchanged. Each track can be muted.  It can work as master or slave with external MIDI clock. The sound generation is based on the MT-32 module, offering 8 melody parts and a rhythm part (MIDI channels 2-9 for melody, 10 for rhythm). It's 32-voice polyphonic, with 128 timbres + 34 rhythm instruments and reverb. Sequencer data is volatile but can be saved to and loaded from a 2.8" quick disk. Sound parameters can be recorded externally via MIDI SysEx data (but not SysEx for sequencer data, only CC).

name: Roland MT-100
description: 4-track sequencer with multitimbral sound generation.  Features 2 main and 2 sub tracks (and a rhythm track), recording is only possible on the main tracks.  Simultaneous recording of data from all MIDI channels on each main track, with the option to mix data from different main tracks afterwards (merge/bounce function).  Data can be exchanged between main and playback-only sub tracks. Individual track muting is possible. Can work as a master or slave synced to an external MIDI clock. Sound generation is based on the MT-32 module with 8 melody parts and a rhythm part using MIDI channels 2-9 (melody) and 10 (rhythm). 32-voice polyphony, 128 sounds + 34 rhythm instruments, and reverb. Sequencer data is volatile (lost after power off), but can be saved and loaded from a Quick-Disk (2.8' disk). Parameter values for sound generation can be recorded externally via MIDI SysEx data.  Records note data and CC data, but not SysEx.

name: Roland MV-30 Studio M, Sequencer with RS-PCM Sound Generation
description: The MV-30 is a combination of a 30-voice, 8-part multitimbral sound engine and a 16-track sequencer in a console-style housing. The sound generation is based on that of the U-20, expanded with the filters of the D-70. A sound program is called a 'Timbre' and is based on a 'Tone,' which is shaped by a dynamic, resonant filter and dynamic amplitude, and modulated by two envelopes and an LFO. A Tone consists of one or two oscillators that play 1 or 2 fixed PCM waveforms, either together, split, or crossfaded by velocity. The MV-30 has 2 slots for PCM cards to expand the internal library of 220 preset tones; cards for the U-series and D-70 can also be used. There are 7 normal synthesizer parts to which 128 storable Timbres can be assigned, and one rhythm part (for rhythm Timbre 129). The 128 Timbres and the rhythm Timbre can be saved together as a set under an 8-character name on a floppy disk. 8 sets can be stored per floppy disk. The sequencer is mainly song-oriented but also offers 20 patterns per song. There are a total of 18 tracks, with 1 track for (MIDI) mixer data and one tempo track not intended for notes. The remaining tracks are divided into 8 single-channel tracks, which are fixed to the internal sound engine parts and cannot output data externally. The last 8 tracks can record mixed data from all 16 MIDI channels and either output them via MIDI or route them to the internal sound engine. Each of the 16 note tracks can also optionally be declared as a pattern track and then call up a pattern sequence. Up to 20 patterns of a song can be assigned as RPS phrases to individual keys (note numbers) and then manually started at any time using the RPS function. Realtime and step input are available as recording methods, and individual events can be edited in detail. Internally, approximately 50,000 events can be recorded; on floppy disk, approximately 70,000-100,000 events can be stored. The maximum number of songs is 20 (internal) or 64 songs (floppy disk). In addition to its own format, the MV-30 can load songs from W-30, MC sequencers (MC-300, MC-500, MC-500MKII, and MC-50), S-samplers (SYS-503, SYS-333, SYS-553), and DOS-formatted SMF disks. Songs can be saved as MV-30, W-30, S-MRC, and SMF songs. The sequencer can operate as a master or as a slave to MIDI Clock and understands the Song Position Pointer. The MV-30 can generate an FSK signal for tape synchronization and can also run as a slave to a tape with FSK.

name: Roland MV-8000 Production Studio
description: The MV-8000 is a combination of sequencer and sampler in a console housing with a built-in hard drive. The sequencer offers 128 tracks, on which, however, only one channel can be recorded at a time. Only from software version 3.5 onwards can patterns be used; otherwise, the sequencer is song-oriented, meaning tracks extend over the entire length of the song. The MV-8000's sampler is based on the structure of the older Roland S-700 series (S-750 / 760, etc.), meaning sampling CD-ROMs for this series can be read and processed directly by the MV-8000. A patch (sound program) consists of up to 128 "partials" (keyboard zones), with each partial able to contain up to four samples that can be crossfaded via a controller or velocity. Samples can include 1 loop, which can be played forwards, backwards, or alternating. All samples for a project must be stored in internal memory, which can be expanded to 512MB with a DIMM. The built-in hard drive is only used for backing up projects.

name: Roland OP-8/OC-8
description: The Roland OP-8 is an interface with CV/Gate inputs and a DCB output. It bridges analog sequencers like the MC-4A or MC-8 and DCB-controllable synthesizers such as the Juno-60 and Jupiter-8. Early Juno-60 and Jupiter-8 models lacked a DCB interface, but the OC-8 retrofit kit added this functionality. The OP-8 provides eight voices with CV and Gate inputs (mini-jack), split into Upper and Lower sections. Each section has CV inputs for VCF and VCA control. A 4-way patch bay with three jacks per section allows signal routing. A transpose switch shifts the octave by +/- 1 octave, and two knobs control the VCF and VCA range. A 'Patch Select' section offers MPX and CV inputs for switching Jupiter-8 patches.

description: The PK-25 full pedal is a MIDI keyboard for the feet without its own sounds, featuring 25 pedals. The pedal sends MIDI notes in the fixed range of note numbers 36 to 60 (C2 to C4) on a fixed MIDI channel 2. The pedal is not velocity-sensitive and sends notes with a fixed velocity of 120. The PK-25 includes an expression pedal with two side buttons, as well as an additional HOLD button. The buttons output MIDI CC messages with fixed CC numbers (18, 19, and 64), while the expression pedal is fixed to Expression (CC#11). A separate output jack is provided for each of these controls to connect the buttons or pedal to the pedal inputs of a master keyboard or organ. If a cable is plugged into one of the jacks, the corresponding MIDI message is no longer transmitted. The PK-25 can be connected to a VK-77 via a special PK connection, which handles all MIDI communication and powers the PK-25.
keywords: Sends MIDI notes from C2 to C4 (note numbers 36-60)
Separate output jacks for buttons and expression pedal (disables MIDI transmission when used)
Special PK connection for Roland VK-77 (MIDI and power)

description: The PK-25 is a MIDI foot keyboard with 25 pedals, transmitting MIDI notes from C2 to C4 (notes 36-60) on MIDI channel 2.  It's not velocity-sensitive and sends notes with a fixed velocity of 120.  It includes a swell pedal, two side-mounted footswitches, and a hold switch that output MIDI CC messages.  It also features individual jacks for each element to connect to a master keyboard or organ.

name: Roland PK-25 25 Pedal Foot Keyboard
description: A MIDI foot keyboard with 25 pedals. It sends MIDI notes in the fixed range of note numbers 36 to 60 (C2 to C4) on MIDI channel 2.  The pedal is not velocity-sensitive and sends notes with a fixed velocity of 120. It includes a volume pedal with two side buttons and an additional HOLD button. The buttons output MIDI CC messages with fixed CC numbers (18, 19, and 64). The volume pedal is fixed to Expression (CC#11). Each control element has a separate output jack to connect to the pedal inputs of a master keyboard or organ. name: Roland PK-5
description: The PK-5 is a MIDI foot keyboard with 13 pedals that typically send notes in the bass range on MIDI channel 2 after power-on. Various buttons let you set the octave, MIDI channel, or note order. You can choose between monophonic and polyphonic modes, and a hold button keeps notes playing after releasing the pedal.
keywords: Controller value sending (CC93, CC92, CC07, CC64)

name: Roland PK-5 MIDI Bass Pedal
description: The PK-5 is a MIDI keyboard for the feet without its own sounds, featuring 13 pedals that typically send notes in the bass range on MIDI Channel 2 after power-on. By pressing various buttons, one can determine that the PK-5 sends notes in different octave ranges, on another MIDI channel, or even notes sorted for E-series arrangers. It can also be set to output only the last played note or to operate polyphonically. The Hold button allows releasing the pressed pedals so that the notes continue to sustain. The PK-5 is velocity-sensitive but can also be switched to a fixed velocity of 64. The MIDI PRG button can be pressed, followed by using the pedals to set a number for a Program Change command, which is sent when the 'H' pedal is pressed to conclude. Additionally, buttons can be activated to send the following Controller values: CC93=On, CC93=Off, CC92=On, CC92=Off, CC07=0,30, 45, 64, 80, 95 or 110, and CC64=On/Off. When the Factory Set button is pressed, the pedals can send sequencer functions like Start, Stop, as well as several control functions relevant to the Roland E-series (Fill In to Variation, Fill In to Original, Break-Mute, Intro, Ending).
keywords: MIDI keyboard with 13 pedals (no internal sounds)
Sends notes on MIDI Channel 2 (bass range) by default

Sends various MIDI Controller (CC) values (CC93, CC92, CC07, CC64)

name: Roland PK-5 MIDI Bass Pedal
description: A MIDI foot keyboard with 13 pedals that usually send notes in the bass range on MIDI channel 2 after power-on. name: Roland PR-1 2-Track MIDI Recorder/Player
description: The PR-1 is a simple 2-track MIDI sequencer without editing functions, but with an integrated library of piano pieces for practice. For personal recordings, approximately 4000 events of memory space are available. Only 1 custom song can be recorded, and data backup is not provided. However, data remains preserved after powering off (as long as the buffer battery still has charge). A metronome can be activated with time signatures of 1-4 half notes, 1 to 8 quarter notes, or 1 to 9 eighth notes, and the tempo can be set from 10 to 250 BPM.

name: Roland PR-100
description: The PR-100 is a simple MIDI sequencer with a 2.8" floppy disk drive, 2 tracks, and 2 sub-tracks that contain the last recording on a main track separately. It also includes a rhythm track where rhythm data from pre-set QDs can be muted separately.  It used the now-obsolete 2.8" QuickDisk format.
keywords: Approximately 17,000 internal events and 8,500 per side of a QD

name: Roland PR-100 MIDI Sequencer
description: The PR-100 is a simple MIDI sequencer with a 2.8" drive, 2 tracks, and 2 so-called subtracks that separately contain the last recording on a main track. In addition, there is a rhythm track on which rhythm data from pre-assigned QDs can be muted separately. Using the merge function and the two main tracks, a complex song can be gradually assembled using the overdub method. The 2.8" QuickDisk drive built into the PR-100, which served to save and load data, was an attempt at the time to introduce a new data storage format in music electronics, but it did not catch on. Unfortunately, these QD drives are also extremely prone to failure, and only a few are still functional today. The PR-100 can store approximately 17,000 events internally and approximately 8,500 per side of a QD. For the PR-100 and the MT-100 (equipped with an additional sound module), an extensive library of QuickDisks with piano pieces for practice was optionally available.
keywords: 2 subtracks (contain last recording on a main track)

name: Roland PR-800
description: The PR-800 is a simple one-track MIDI sequencer and recorder designed for use with HP-300/HP-400 MIDI pianos. Recording is real-time only, with basic editing capabilities for time correction in 3/4 or 4/4 time. Playback allows for looping of the entire sequence or sections thereof.  Data could be saved to tape via FSK.

name: Roland PR-800 MIDI Digital Recorder "RECORDER PLUS"
description: The PR-800 is a simple 1-track MIDI sequencer designed as a MIDI recorder for MIDI pianos. Recording is exclusively in real-time. If a time signature of 3/4 or 4/4 is set beforehand, the recording can be corrected measure by measure; otherwise, there are no further editing options. For playback, repetition of either the entire sequence or a specific range can be set. Tempo is adjusted via a rotary knob. The PR-800 can act as a MIDI Clock master or slave, and recorded data can be saved to tape/cassette using an FSK signal. No information on storage capacity is provided.
keywords: Roland PR-800 MIDI Digital Recorder "RECORDER PLUS"

name: Roland RS-09 Organ Strings
description: The RS-09 'Organ Strings 09' is a 44-key analog keyboard combining an organ and a string ensemble in a compact housing.  The keyboard is not velocity-sensitive. The string section offers two foot positions (8 and 4) and has a controller for the attack time. The organ section has 4 controllers for mixing the foot positions (16, 8, 4, and 2). In each section, the ensemble effect can be switched on/off, and the reverb can be adjusted with the common release controller. There is also a common vibrato control, a tone controller for sound adjustment, and a selector switch for Ensemble I or II.  The rear panel features stereo outputs, stereo headphone jack, a separate organ output (mono), and a gate control output. There's also a sustain pedal input and an audio input for using the ensemble effect with external sound sources.
keywords: String section with 2 foot positions and attack control
Organ section with 4 foot position mixing controllers

name: Roland RS-09 Organ-Strings
description: The RS-09 'Organ Strings 09' is a 44-key analog keyboard combining an organ and a string ensemble in a compact housing. The keyboard is not velocity-sensitive. The string section offers two footages (8' and 4') and an attack time control. The organ section offers 4 controls for mixing footages (16', 8', 4', and 2'). In each section, the ensemble effect can be switched on/off, and the decay can be adjusted with the common Release control. There is also a common Vibrato control, a Tone control for sound shaping, and a selector switch for Ensemble I or II. On the rear panel, there are stereo outputs, a stereo headphone jack, a separate mono organ output, and a gate control output. A sustain pedal input and an audio input for using the ensemble effect with external sound sources are also present. Like the VP-330, there was an early version with grey rocker switches and later with illuminated, colorful buttons, known from the Jupiter-8.
keywords: Combines organ and string ensemble sections
String section: 8' and 4' footages, Attack time control
Organ section: 16', 8', 4', and 2' footage mixing controls
Switchable Ensemble effect for each section
Audio input for external sound sources to use the ensemble effect
Early versions with grey rocker switches, later with illuminated buttons

name: Roland RS-101
description: The Roland RS-101 is a polyphonic, analog keyboard with 61 non-velocity-sensitive keys that produce string imitations.  It features two keyboard zones with independently switchable sounds (3 total sounds).  Each sound has individual tone controls, and a global vibrato effect is adjustable in intensity.  Each zone has a volume attenuator and attack time selector (Slow/Fast). It has two line outputs but no headphone output.

name: Roland RS-101 String-Ensemble, Keyboard Synthesizer
description: The Roland Strings RS-101 is a polyphonic, analog keyboard with 61 non-velocity-sensitive keys designed to produce string emulations. The RS-101 is permanently built into an instrument case with a detachable lid. It features two keyboard zones for which a total of 3 sounds (Brass, two String sounds) can be independently enabled and disabled. The Brass sound and the two String sounds can be separately adjusted in tone, and a fixed-frequency vibrato's intensity can be controlled for the entire keyboard. For each keyboard zone, the volume can be slightly attenuated with a rocker switch, and the attack time can be switched between Slow and Fast. A master volume control is present. There are no further sound shaping settings. There is no headphone output, only two line outputs that carry the same mono signal at higher and lower levels. Unlike other string ensembles of its time, the RS-101 has independent envelopes for individual voices.
keywords: Built into an instrument case with detachable lid
3 sounds (Brass, two String sounds) independently switchable per zone
Separate tone control for Brass and String sounds
Rocker switch for volume dampening and attack time (Slow/Fast) per zone

name: Roland RS-202
description: The Roland RS-202 String Ensemble is a polyphonic analog keyboard with 61 non-velocity-sensitive keys designed for creating string sounds.  Housed in a hard case with a removable lid, it offers two keyboard zones, each with independent on/off control for its three sounds (brass and two string variations). The brass and string sounds can be individually adjusted, and a fixed-frequency vibrato with adjustable intensity is available for the entire keyboard. Each zone also has a switch for slightly dampening volume and toggling attack time between slow and fast.  The RS-202 adds an ensemble switch (off, I, and II), providing a Roland chorus effect, and a delayed vibrato compared to its predecessor, the RS-101.  It lacks a headphone output, offering two line outputs carrying the same mono signal at different levels.

name: Roland RS-202 String Ensemble
description: The Roland Strings RS-202 is a polyphonic, analog keyboard with 61 non-velocity-sensitive keys for generating string imitations. The RS-202 is firmly built into the instrument case, and the lid can be removed. It has two keyboard zones, for which the three sounds can be switched on and off independently. The brass sound and the two string sounds can be adjusted separately, and a fixed-frequency vibrato can be adjusted in intensity for the entire keyboard. For each keyboard zone, the volume can be slightly dampened with a rocker switch, and the attack time can be switched between slow and fast. A controller is available for the overall volume. Compared to its predecessor, the RS-101, the ability to delay the vibrato and the ensemble switch with 3 positions (bypass, I, and II) have been added. This is the typical Roland chorus effect.
keywords: Adjustable sound parameters for each sound

name: Roland RS-505
description: The RS-505 is a 49-key analog synthesizer with three sound generation sections (bass, synthesizer, strings) and two keyboard zones (upper and lower).  The bass section is monophonic with three selectable sounds (contrabass, tuba, cello) and an adjustable AR envelope. The polyphonic synthesizer section has fixed registers, a filter with cutoff frequency and resonance, and an LFO or ADSR envelope modulation. The polyphonic string section offers adjustable mixes of 8' and 4' strings for each zone.  It includes an LFO, vibrato, ensemble effect, autobend, and more.

name: Roland RS-505 String Paraphonic 505
description: 49-key keyboard with 3 sound generation sections and two keyboard zones (Upper and Lower), split point at middle C. Bass section: monophonic synthesizer with 3 switchable sounds (Contra Bass 16, Tuba 8, Cello 8) and adjustable AR envelope. Polyphonic Synthesizer section: fixed registers (Bass 16, Bass 8, Lower 8, Lower 4, Upper 8, Upper 4), filter with adjustable cutoff frequency and resonance, modulation by LFO or ADSR envelope. Polyphonic String section: per zone (Upper/Lower), slider for adjusting the mix ratio of 8' and 4' strings and a rocker switch for on/off.  Effects include Ensemble, Attack, Vibrato, Autobend, and more. Outputs: Stereo, Synth-Bass, Trigger, Gate. Inputs: Ext IN, Pitch, Sustain, VCF.
keywords: Filter with Adjustable Cutoff Frequency and Resonance

name: Roland RS-505 String Paraphonic 505, Keyboard Synthesizer
description: Named 'Paraphonic 505' on its casing, the RS-505 is an analog 49-key keyboard with 3 sound generation sections and two keyboard zones, Upper and Lower, featuring a fixed split point at middle C. The Bass section consists of a monophonic synthesizer with 3 switchable sounds (Contra Bass 16, Tuba 8, and Cello 8) and an adjustable AR envelope. Its volume can be set via a slider, and the global Ensemble effect can be activated. The polyphonic 'Synthesizer' section also has fixed registers (Bass 16, Bass 8, Lower 8, Lower 4, Upper 8, and Upper 4), but offers a filter with adjustable cutoff frequency and resonance, which can be modulated by an LFO or an ADSR envelope. Unfortunately, the RS-505 has only a single envelope generator for all voices, meaning the envelope is only triggered when all keys have been released beforehand. The Ensemble effect can be activated for the entire synthesizer section. The volume of the synthesizer section can be set as a balance to the String section for both the Upper and Lower parts. The polyphonic String section offers a slider per zone (Upper/Lower) to adjust the mix ratio of 8' and 4' strings and a rocker switch to activate/deactivate that zone. For the Strings, in addition to the switchable Ensemble effect, there is an Attack control, which, like in the synthesizer section, only takes effect with staccato playing. Therefore, both the String and Synthesizer sections should actually be described as homophonic rather than polyphonic. Furthermore, there is an LFO adjustable in rate and delay, an adjustable vibrato, a switch for the Ensemble effect (I, II, or off), an adjustable Autobend function or manual pitch lowering by up to an octave, and controls for overall tuning and volume. On the rear, the RS-505 has the following outputs: Stereo Output, Synth Bass Output (when connected, takes bass and synthesizer bass sounds out of the stereo output), Trigger and Gate Output. Ext IN (audio input located before the Ensemble effect), Pitch (toggles transpose on/off), Sustain (hold function), and VCF (control input for pedal) are the available inputs.

Single envelope generator for all voices (homophonic operation)

An LFO, vibrato, ensemble effect (I, II, or off), autobend function, and pitch lowering are also available. name: Roland S-10
description: The Roland S-10 is an 8-voice sampler with 49 velocity-sensitive keys, an arpeggiator, and a 2.8-inch floppy disk drive (Quick Disk format). It samples at 12-bit resolution and 15 or 30kHz sample rates. It has 256kB of internal memory divided into four 64kB banks, allowing for a total sample time of about 4.4 seconds. Samples can be edited, looped, and have a dynamics envelope applied. It only has a single MIDI part.
keywords: Sample editing, looping, and dynamics envelope

name: Roland S-10 MIDI SAMPLER, 49 keys and 2.8" Floppy Drive
description: The Roland S-10 'Digital Sampling Keyboard' is an 8-voice sampler with 49 velocity-sensitive keys, an arpeggiator, and a 2.8-inch floppy drive (Quick Disk format, or QD). The S-10 samples at 12-bit resolution and either 15 or 30kHz. The internal memory of 256kB is divided into 4 banks of 64kB each, so all samples combined can be a maximum of 4.4 seconds long, approximately 1.1 seconds per bank. To record a 'long' sample, two banks can be combined. Samples can be edited on the device, assigned a dynamic envelope, and looped, but there is no dynamic filter. A maximum of 4 samples can be arranged side-by-side (split) or layered across the keyboard. The S-10 has only one (MIDI) part. Monitor and mouse operation, like on its 'big brother' S-50, is not provided; the S-10's controls and single-line display must suffice here.

name: Roland S-220 Digital Sampler
description: The Roland S-220 Digital Sampler is a 16-voice sampler module in 19-inch format with 2U and a built-in 2.8-inch floppy disk drive (Quick-Disk format, QD). It samples with 12-bit and either 15 or 30kHz, but already has 16-bit A/D converters. The internal memory of 256kB is divided into 4 banks of 64kb each, so that all samples together can be a maximum of 4.4 seconds long, approximately 1.1 seconds per bank. To record a 'long' sample, two banks can be combined. Samples can be edited in the device, provided with a dynamic envelope, and looped; however, there is no dynamic filter. The S-220 reads QuickDisks from S-10 and MKS-100, so it is data-compatible with the L-100 series. The S-220 operates in MIDI mono mode, where up to 8 consecutive channels can be used, or up to 4-fold multitimbral in poly mode, where voice allocation is not dynamic but must be preselected. In poly mode, the note range per channel can be limited. Monitor and mouse operation like in the 'big brothers' S-50, S-330 is not provided; here, the operating elements of the S-220 and the two-line display must suffice.

description: The Roland S-330 is a 16-voice digital sampler module with a 3.5-inch floppy drive for sample storage.  It's similar to the S-50 keyboard sampler, offering dynamic filters but only one memory bank (similar to the S-50).  It samples at 12-bit with 15 or 30kHz sampling rates.  It supports up to 32 samples, which can be arranged into 16 patches.

name: Roland S-330 19" Sampler Module
description: The S-330 is a 16-voice digital sampler module with 1U rack size and a 3.5-inch floppy drive for sample storage. Essentially, the S-330 is the module counterpart to the S-50 keyboard sampler; while the S-330 has dynamic filters, it only has one memory, exactly like the S-50, unlike the S-550. The memory holds a maximum of 2 x 7.2 seconds of samples, divided into banks A and B. The S-330 samples at 12-bit with a selectable rate of 15 or 30kHz, but sounds excellent thanks to its superb 16-bit converters. The sound basis consists of a maximum of 32 pure samples, which are assigned playback parameters to become "Tones". Tones can be freely distributed across the keyboard and saved as a Patch (sound program). The S-330 allows for 16 patches. The small display is not inviting for editing, but a monitor, mouse, and a tablet for drawing waveforms (DT-100) can be connected. The operating system must be loaded from a floppy disk at startup. The S-330 has no option for a SCSI interface but can also transform into a multi-track MIDI sequencer using the optional, hardware-dongle-protected DIRECTOR-S software SYS-333.
keywords: Memory divided into banks A and B
Connectivity for monitor, mouse, and DT-100 tablet
Operating system must be loaded from floppy disk
Optional multi-track MIDI sequencer via DIRECTOR-S software SYS-333

name: Roland S-50
description: The Roland S-50 is a 16-voice digital sampler with a 61-key velocity-sensitive keyboard and a 3.5-inch floppy drive for sample storage.  It was Roland's first sampler to offer storage for 2 x 7.2 seconds of samples at 15 or 30kHz sampling rates.  The memory is not expandable. name: Roland S-750 Professional Digital Stereo Sampler
description: The Roland S-750 is a 24-voice, 16-bit stereo sampler with mouse and monitor connection. Sampling frequencies of 22.05, 44.1, or 48 kHz can be used. The S-750 must load its operating system at startup, either from a floppy disk or from SCSI-connected storage devices. The S-750 can be fully operated with its built-in display and buttons, though this is somewhat cumbersome. Alternatively, a monitor (or TV with S-Video input) and a mouse (MU-1), and optionally a remote control (RC-100), can be connected for a very comfortable user experience. The sound generation is structured as follows: A sample includes loop points and loop mode (forward, reverse, alternate, no loop), original pitch, and fine-tuning. Up to 4 samples can be assigned to a partial, which controls panorama, level, dynamic crossfading with fades, etc. Dynamic amplifiers, filters, envelopes, and LFOs are also part of the partial. Up to 88 partials can be distributed as non-overlapping zones across the note range (splits) to form a patch (sound program of a part). Up to 32 parts can be assigned MIDI channels and output routing to form a performance. For data storage, there is also the "Volume," which groups multiple performances and can be loaded into the S-750's memory at once. The factory memory is 2MB but can be expanded to a total of 18MB. This requires installing the RAS-750 memory expansion board, which then accepts OMS-750 memory modules. The S-750 is fully data-compatible with the S-770 and can also handle data from the S-760. One of these three samplers (S-750, S-770, or S-760) or the sample player SP-700 is referred to when speaking of the Roland S-700 series, for which there is a large library of samples from other manufacturers as well as from Roland itself.

description: The SH-1 is a compact, monophonic analog synthesizer with 32 (non-velocity-sensitive) keys. The single VCO can generate square, sawtooth, or modifiable pulse waves and can be mixed in the Audio Mixer section with signals from the sub-oscillator and a separate noise generator. A static high-pass filter and a dynamic low-pass filter, as well as a VCA, are controlled by an ADSR or AR envelope. For modulation, an LFO, Portamento, and a Pitch Bend lever are available. There are no audio effects, but CV/Gate inputs and outputs, as well as an external audio and a trigger input, are provided.

name: Roland SH-1000
description: The SH-1000 is Roland's first synthesizer. It's an analog monophonic synthesizer. Users can select from 10 preset sounds or manually adjust the sound. It doesn't have any memory for custom settings.  The sound generation consists of a VCO, VCF (low-pass with resonance), and VCA. It has an ADSR envelope generator and three fixed curves for the VCA. It does not have a headphone jack, audio effects, or CV/Gate connectors.

name: Roland SH-101 Monophonic Synthesizer
description: The Roland SH-101 is a monophonic analog synthesizer that became a staple for basslines and lead sounds in electronic music. It features a single voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO), a sub-oscillator, a noise generator, a resonant low-pass filter (VCF), and an envelope generator, all contributing to its distinctive raw, punchy sound. It also includes a simple step sequencer and an arpeggiator, which can be synced to external clock sources. The compact design and optional handgrip/mod-grip made it portable and performable.

name: Roland SH-2 Monophonic Synthesizer with 2 Oscillators
description: The SH-2 is a compact, monophonic analog synthesizer with 37 (non-velocity-sensitive) keys. Both VCOs can be set to footages of 32, 16, 8, 4, and 2, and waveforms of sawtooth, square, and pulse. VCO-1 additionally offers sine and has a mixable sub-oscillator, while VCO-2, which can be detuned against VCO-1, also offers noise. The subsequent dynamic 24dB low-pass filter is equipped with controllable resonance up to self-oscillation and shares its ADSR envelope with the final VCA, which can also be controlled by Gate or Hold. Modulation options include an LFO, portamento, and the pitch bend lever. There are no audio effects, but CV/Gate inputs and outputs, as well as an external audio input, are present.

description: The SH-2000 is a monophonic, analog preset synthesizer with 37 non-velocity-sensitive keys.  The keyboard offers a type of aftertouch to control vibrato, pitch bend, or a growl effect.  Its 30 presets allow modification of parameters like envelope sustain, modulation strength and rate, filter cutoff, and resonance, but completely custom settings aren't possible. It uses one oscillator and lacks audio effects, headphone or control connections, and uses a logarithmic voltage/Hertz control in contrast to other Roland synthesizers.

name: Roland SH-2000 Monophonic Analog Synthesizer

For the 30 sounds stored in the presets, parameters such as envelope sustain, modulation intensity, modulation rate, filter cutoff, and resonance can be changed, but completely custom settings are not possible. The SH-2000 generates sounds with a single oscillator, has no audio effects, no headphone or control connections, and, unlike other Roland synthesizers, utilizes logarithmic Volt/Hertz control.

name: Roland SH-5
description: The SH-5 is a substantial, monophonic analog synthesizer equipped with 44 non-velocity-sensitive keys, permanently integrated into a flight case with an angled control surface. It features two VCOs, each offering selectable triangle, sawtooth, square, and modulatable pulse waveforms, which can be ring-modulated and mixed with adjustable noise. The sound passes through a fixed bandpass filter, a dynamic multi-filter (Hi, Band, or Low), and a VCA, with the envelope shaped by an ADSR and an AR generator. Modulation is provided by Portamento, two LFOs, a Sample & Hold generator, and the innovative pitch bend lever, first introduced with the SH-5. It offers extensive control connections but no built-in audio effects.

name: Roland SH-5 Synthesizer
description: The SH-5 is a heavy, monophonic analog synthesizer with 44 non-velocity-sensitive keys built into a flight case with an angled control panel.  It features two VCOs with selectable waveforms (triangle, sawtooth, square, pulse), ring modulation, a noise generator, a fixed bandpass filter, a dynamic multi-filter, and a VCA.  It also includes ADSR and AR envelopes, portamento, two LFOs, a sample and hold generator, and a pitch bend lever.  No audio effects are present, but multiple control inputs are available.

name: Roland SH-7
description: The SH-7 is a two-voice analog synthesizer with 44 non-velocity-sensitive keys, built into a flight case lower section and featuring an angled control panel. It has two oscillators, both independently adjustable in octave (2, 4, 8, 16, 32) and waveform (triangle, sawtooth, square, and pulse width modulation). Only VCO1 also provides a freely adjustable 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 octave mixture of square waves. VCO2 can be synchronized to VCO1 or used when playing two-voice on the keyboard.  Mixable noise and a ring modulator complete the sound generation, which is shaped by a fixed high-pass filter and the dynamic VCF and VCA blocks. Two envelopes are available. Modulation is possible using the pitch bend lever, LFO, and a random generator. CV/Gate inputs and outputs are also available, as well as an external audio input, headphone jack and control input for the filter frequency.

name: Roland System 100M 110
description: The Roland System 100M 110 is a combined VCO, VCF, and VCA module. This module combines the three main synthesizer elements: voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO), voltage-controlled filter (VCF), and voltage-controlled amplifier (VCA).  In conjunction with the 140 module (ENV 1/2, LFO), it provides all necessary components for sound generation. The combination of modules 110 and 140 allows for control of each individual function.  The VCO, VCF, and VCA are internally hardwired, reducing external connections. However, all internal connections are automatically interrupted when external connections are used.  The 110 module can be controlled by the 140's envelope generator.

name: Roland TR-808
description: The Roland Rhythm Composer TR-808 is an analog, pattern-oriented drum machine. Its 16 sounds can be routed through individual outputs and their tone, decay, or pitch can sometimes be adjusted. The sound is very powerful and should be well-known. Unlike all previous Roland rhythm machines, the TR-808 has no preset rhythms, but is "only" freely programmable. However, upon delivery, 3 tracks were pre-assigned, which can be deleted. A maximum of 12 songs, called tracks here, with 64 patterns each, can be stored. The TR-808 can be synchronized via DIN-SYNC with other DIN-SYNC devices and additionally outputs three trigger signals, which depend on the programming of the "Cowbell", "Clap" or "Maraca" instruments and the accent. The simple pattern programming via "lauflichtsteuerung" (step sequencing) is pioneering, where each 16th note (or 8th note) of a 4/4 bar corresponds to one of the illuminated 16 buttons, and the selected instrument (bass drum, snare, hi-hat, etc.) can be set or removed by simply pressing it at the corresponding beat. When notes are set, the corresponding button lights up. This allows for very comfortable rhythm input. After Roland introduced programmability with the CR-78 and achieved great success, the Boss DR-55 was the first rhythm machine without fixed rhythms on the market, but it offered little memory. The TR-808 offers this memory capability and is, so to speak, the big brother of the DR-55.

name: Roland TR-808
description: The Roland TR-808 Rhythm Composer is an analog, pattern-based drum computer. Its 16 sounds can be output via individual outputs and sometimes modified in sound, decay, or pitch. The sound is very powerful and should be familiar to most.  Unlike earlier Roland rhythm machines, the TR-808 has no preset rhythms; it's purely freely programmable. However, 3 tracks were pre-loaded upon delivery, but these can be deleted. A maximum of 12 songs (called tracks here), each with 64 patterns, can be stored. The TR-808 can be synchronized with other DIN-SYNC devices via DIN-SYNC and also outputs three trigger signals that depend on the programming of the "Cowbell", "Clap", and "Maraca" instruments and the accent.

It has a 24-pin input and two 24-pin outputs.  It can also be used with a G-33 or G-88 and two GR-33B or GR-77B bass synthesizers. However, it cannot distribute two guitars/basses to one synthesizer or combine guitar and bass components.

name: Roland US-20
description: The Roland US-20 is a switch and distributor for use with a GK guitar (guitar with GK-2, GK-2A(H), or GK-3) to control two 13-pin devices, such as GR synthesizers (e.g., GR-09, GR-1, GR-20, GR-33), Guitar-to-MIDI converters (e.g., GI-10, GI-20), or Virtual Guitar systems (e.g., VG-8, VG-88, VG-99). It has a 13-pin input and two 13-pin outputs.  It also works with GK-2B/GK-3B equipped bass guitars and two GK bass devices. Power is supplied via the 13-pin cable from one of the connected GK devices.
keywords: switches for selecting and combining devices

name: Roland US-20 Unit Selector
description: The Roland US-20 is a switch and splitter that allows a GK-equipped guitar (with GK-2, GK-2A(H), or GK-3) to control two 13-pin devices simultaneously.  This includes GR synthesizers like the GR-09, GR-1, GR-20, GR-33, guitar-to-MIDI converters like the GI-10, GI-20, or virtual guitar systems like the VG-8, VG-88, VG-99. The rear panel has a 13-pin input and two 13-pin outputs, and the top panel has two switches. The left switch selects between device A or B, and the right switch adds the other device if you want to play both simultaneously. LEDs indicate the switching status. Power is supplied via the 13-pin cable from one of the connected GK devices.  The US-20 can also be used for a bass with a GK-2B or GK-3B pickup and two GK bass devices (e.g., GI-20, V-Bass, or VB-99).
keywords: Simultaneous output to two GK devices

name: Roland W-30
description: The Roland W-30 Music Workstation is a 16-voice digital sampler featuring a velocity-sensitive 61-key keyboard, a 3.5-inch floppy drive for sample storage, and a built-in sequencer comparable to the MC-500.  It offers 2 x 7.2 seconds of sampling time at 30kHz or 2 x 14.4 seconds at 15kHz, with a fixed sample memory.  While using 12-bit resolution (carried over from the S-50), its high-quality 16-bit converters contribute to a good overall sound.  Up to 32 raw samples can be combined with playback parameters to create "tones," which can be mapped across the keyboard and saved as patches (up to 16). The W-30 also features dynamic filters like the S-330 and S-550. The sequencer includes a tempo track and 16 MIDI tracks, each capable of recording data on all 16 MIDI channels. It can also load song data from the Director S sequencers of other S-series samplers, the MC-500, and Super-MRC.  Data is stored on the internal 3.5-inch floppy drive or an external SCSI hard drive (up to 80MB) via the optional KW-30 SCSI interface board.  Like other S-series samplers, the operating system needs to be loaded from disk upon startup.
keywords: Compatible with Director S sequencer files

name: Roland W-30 Sampler Workstation
description: The W-30 'Music Workstation' is a 16-voice digital sampler with a velocity-sensitive 61-key keyboard, a 3.5-inch floppy drive for sample storage, and a built-in sequencer comparable to the MC-500. The sample memory, offering 2 x 7.2 seconds at 30kHz or 2 x 14.4 seconds at 15kHz samples, is not expandable. The 12-bit resolution inherited from the S-50 is compensated by very good 16-bit converters, resulting in a relatively good sound for the W-30. The sound basis consists of a maximum of 32 pure samples, which are combined with playback parameters to form 'Tones.' Tones can be freely distributed across the keyboard and saved as Patches (sound programs). The W-30 allows for creating 16 Patches. Like the S-330 and S-550, the W-30 has dynamic filters. The sequencer features a tempo track and 16 MIDI tracks, with each track able to record data on all 16 MIDI channels. The W-30 can read song data from Director S sequencers of other S-samplers, MC-500, and Super-MRC. Operation is performed via various buttons and a combination of cursor wheel and value wheel. Visual feedback is provided by an 8-line liquid crystal display with waveform representation. However, operation is not as comfortable as with other samplers where a mouse and monitor can be connected. Data storage uses the built-in 3.5-inch floppy drive or an external hard drive (SCSI, max 80MB!), provided the KW-30 SCSI interface is installed and a functional hard drive is connected. As with all other S-samplers, the operating system must first be loaded from a data medium after power-on.

name: S-220 Sampler Module with 2.8" Quickdisk
description: The Roland S-220 'Digital Sampler' is a 16-voice sampler module in 19-inch rack format (2U height) with a built-in 2.8-inch floppy drive (Quick Disk format, or QD). The S-220 samples at 12-bit resolution and either 15 kHz or 30 kHz, but already features 16-bit A/D converters. The internal memory of 256KB is divided into 4 banks of 64KB each, allowing for a maximum total sample length of 4.4 seconds, or approximately 1.1 seconds per bank. Two banks can be combined for longer samples. Samples can be edited within the device, assigned a dynamic envelope, and looped; however, there is no dynamic filter. The S-220 can read Quick Disks from the S-10 and MKS-100, making it data-compatible with the L-100 series. The S-220 operates in MIDI Mono mode, where up to 8 consecutive channels can be used, or up to 4-part multitimbral in Poly mode, though voice distribution is not dynamic and must be pre-selected. In Poly mode, the note range can be limited per channel. Monitor and mouse operation, as seen on its 'bigger brothers' S-50 and S-330, is not provided; the S-220's front panel controls and two-line display are used for operation. In February 1987, the S-220 was announced under the name MKS-200, but all production models were called S-220.

description: The SBX-80 is a Sync Box used for common tempo control of connected MIDI devices (MIDI Clock), DIN-Sync devices, and those requiring trigger impulses, supporting 1, 2, 3, 4, 12, 24, 28, or 96 impulses per quarter note. The tempo of the SBX-80 can be entered in Manual mode via a rotary knob or tapped in via the TAP button. Additionally, up to 8 tempo sequences for songs can be programmed. In Slave mode, only the programmed songs can be run, with SMPTE or MIDI Clock selectable as synchronization sources. The SBX-80 can also generate SMPTE code. Real-time conversion from DIN-Sync or trigger to MIDI Clock, etc., is not possible, especially since there is no DIN Sync input.

name: SH-09 Monophonic Synthesizer
description: The SH-09 is a compact, monophonic analog synthesizer with 32 (non-velocity-sensitive) keys. One VCO can alternatively produce square, pulse, sawtooth, or noise waveforms, with a sub-oscillator mixable in one or two octaves lower. The sound is shaped by a dynamic 24dB low-pass filter with resonance (up to self-oscillation) and a dynamic amplifier, which share a single ADSR envelope. The VCA can also be controlled by Gate or Hold. For modulation, an LFO, portamento, and pitch bend lever are available. There are no audio effects, but CV/Gate inputs and outputs, as well as an external audio input, are present.
keywords: Dynamic 24dB low-pass filter with resonance (up to self-oscillation)

name: SH-2000 Monophoner Analog-Synthesizer mit Preset-Sounds
description: The SH-2000 is a monophonic, analog preset synthesizer with 37 (non-velocity-sensitive) keys. The keyboard offers a form of aftertouch, which can control effects such as vibrato, pitch bend, or a 'growl' effect. For the 30 sounds stored in the presets, parameters such as envelope sustain, modulation strength, modulation rate, filter cutoff, and filter resonance can be changed; completely custom settings are not possible. The SH-2000 generates sounds with a single oscillator, has no audio effects, no headphone or control connections, and, unlike all other Roland synthesizers, features logarithmic Volt/Hertz control.
keywords: Adjustable parameters for presets: envelope sustain, modulation strength/rate, filter cutoff/resonance

name: SH-3 Monophonic Analog Synthesizer with 44 keys
description: The SH-3 is a monophonic analog synthesizer with 44 (non-velocity-sensitive) keys, built into a flight case. The SH-3 features one VCO, where waveforms (square, pulse, sawtooth, and noise) are mixable and routed through a dynamic 12dB filter with resonance (up to self-oscillation) and a dynamic amplifier (VCA). The VCA can be controlled by two fixed curves or the single ADSR envelope. Two LFOs are available for modulation. There are no audio effects or CV/Gate control connections. Initially, the SH-3 was available under the company name ACE-TONE, and later in 1973 (after the company's founding in 1972), it was also sold under the Roland brand name. With minor circuit changes, the synthesizer was mostly sold as the Roland SH-3A.
